item.content:encoded:
DALLAS, Sept. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Apex Dental Partners, a dental partnership organization supporting dentists and affiliated practices, has been named No. 3,850 on the Inc. 5000 list of America's fastest-growing private companies, marking its eighth consecutive year on the list. The company achieved 67% revenue growth over the past three years, reflecting its continued investment in the doctors, teams, and practices it supports.
Published annually by Inc. magazine, the Inc. 5000 ranks privately held U.S. companies by percentage revenue growth over a three-year period. Apex's eight consecutive appearances reflect steady expansion while preserving its commitment to relationship-based dentistry.
Apex's approach to growth centers on supporting doctor partners personally and professionally through a community of colleagues, coaching, tools, technology, and education. "This recognition belongs to our doctor partners and their teams," said Matt Hale, President of Apex Dental Partners. "The growth we're celebrating this year is the direct result of their hard work, leadership, and commitment to their patients and communities."
That same long-term perspective guides Apex's plans for continued growth. "As we look ahead, our focus stays on building long-term partnerships, investing in our doctors, and staying true to the values of private practice," said David Lohmann, CEO of Apex. "That's the foundation we'll keep growing from."
About Apex Dental Partners
Apex Dental Partners is a dental partnership reimagining private practice dentistry for the next generation of clinicians committed to long-term, relationship-based, high-quality patient care. Through its non-branded Private Practice Reimagined® model, Apex combines the values of traditional dentistry with the resources and support of a larger organization. For more information, visit www.ApexDP.com
SOURCE Apex Dental Partners

item.content:encoded:
Years after her divorce from Armie Hammer, Elizabeth Chambers is uncovering crazy, shocking, and deeply disturbing true stories of love gone horrible wrong in her docuseries “Toxic.”
“Extra” spoke with Elizabeth, a mother-of-two turned TV journalist, said she is excited about the new season.
She said, “It is eye-opening and without shedding light on this, we can’t have a conversation and avoid toxic relationships.”
This season investigates the murder of a University of Virginia lacrosse player, abusive relationships, and even allegations against a preacher.
Chambers revealed some of the red flags to watch out for when a relationship can turn toxic.
She shared, “It is moving too quickly. You know, we do not need to accelerate any relationships for any reason. Let’s take it slowly. Mirroring, if someone is very much showing interest in the same things that you’re interested in and all of a sudden, trying to assimilate themselves into your life, that’s a really big red flag.”
“Toxic” is streaming now on Investigation Discovery and HBO Max.

item.title: [si.com] Trail Blazers Are at the Top of the List to Fall Out of the NBA Playoffs. Here’s Why.
item.dc:creator: Blake Silverman
item.description: - Editor’s Note: For the upcoming Sports Illustrated 2026–27 basketball preview magazine that will hit newsstands in October, SI spoke to anonymous scouts around the NBA about all 30 teams. Portland punched above its weight in the Western Conference last season as the Trail Blazers earned the No. 7 seed with a 42–40 playoff record and a win over the Suns to open the play-in tournament. item.content:encoded:
- Editor’s Note: For the upcoming Sports Illustrated 2026–27 basketball preview magazine that will hit newsstands in October, SI spoke to anonymous scouts around the NBA about all 30 teams.
Portland punched above its weight in the Western Conference last season as the Trail Blazers earned the No. 7 seed with a 42–40 playoff record and a win over the Suns to open the play-in tournament. The Trail Blazers could fall out of the playoff mix this season, however.
Deni Avdija led the way last season in his breakout campaign, dropping 24.2 points per game and earning his first All-Star nod. He helped the Blazers have a say in the stacked conference following a sudden coaching change to start the year. Despite Tiago Splitter’s success as interim coach, Blazers owner Tom Dundon’s cost-cutting measures led to another coaching change over the offseason.
Longtime NBA assistant Micah Nori, who was most recently at the top of Chris Finch’s staff in Minnesota, is the new head man for the Blazers. Dundon didn’t want to put considerable funds into a head coach, which led to Splitter departing for the Bulls. Nori is a good hire, but he only has one guaranteed season on his three-year deal with team options on the final two seasons, which makes it difficult to build something sustainable on an already wonky roster.
“I don’t like how things look in Portland,” an anonymous NBA scout told Sports Illustrated. “Bad ownership, a coach with a bad contract and bad players together. Bad fits. Everything in Portland is a bad fit right now, top to bottom. They have got some guys. I like Toumani Camara. I like Shaedon Sharpe, when he is healthy. But if you are asking me which team falls out of the playoffs, they are at the top of the list.”
On the court, the guard room is extremely crowded, which will force general manager Joe Cronin to make decisions sooner rather than later. The move to buy low on Ja Morant could define Portland’s season, although he was acquired for the low cost of salary filler. A fresh start could do wonders for Morant, but he steps into a backcourt alongside Jrue Holiday, Scoot Henderson and Damian Lillard, who will return this season after rehabbing a torn Achilles.
- Anonymous scouts break down each Western Conference team: Clippers | Grizzlies | Jazz | Kings | Lakers | Mavericks | Nuggets | Pelicans | Rockets | Spurs | Suns | Thunder | Timberwolves | Trail Blazers | Warriors
Morant has played 79 total games over the past three seasons as he’s dealt with injuries and a number of off-court issues that led to a messy breakup with the Grizzlies. When available, he’s an electric finisher who can make plays for his teammates, but the issue is Lillard and Avdija also need the ball in their hands. Plus, the Blazers need to figure out if Henderson is a part of their future as he’s headed for restricted free agency next summer.
“We will probably see a more available Ja. He might play in games,” the scout told SI. “He's got a bad knee, doesn't really work on his physical fitness, I doubt that he's all of a sudden become an elite-level shooter, and he's small. So you have that, you've got a bad defender who's a small guard who can't shoot, who physically is unfit, paired next to a small guard who's a bad defender and who can shoot [in Lillard]. So probably going to be tough.”
On the bright side, Avdija is currently on one of the best contracts in the NBA. However, he’s eligible for a contract extension and will be due for a massive payday should his play continue. That wrinkle should keep a heavy load of on-ball work for Avdija, which makes the slew of guards even more questionable. Sharpe will miss considerable time with a torn meniscus, which gives Nori additional minutes to work with as he figures out which backcourt combinations work best. Losing Sharpe is a big loss, but by the time he’s healthy, maybe Portland will have figured out the guard conundrum—possibly through a trade to consolidate the backcourt depth into a much-needed wings.
The issue? Holiday and Morant’s contracts would be incredibly difficult to get off of.
- NBA Championship Power Rankings: Where Does Your Favorite Team Stack Up?
Down low, Donovan Clingan was one of the NBA’s best rebounders last year in just his second season. He’s an elite rim protector, too, but he still has some work to do to prove he’s worthy of a considerable rookie extension, which he’s eligible for next summer.
“Defensively, [the Blazers] need a DPOY type of year from Clingan,” the scout said. “I think he has some upside and can be pretty impactful. Still got to improve his fitness level, but I thought he showed growth from year one to year two, and he continues on that he's probably going to be a nice player. But he is going to have a lot of work to do defending against dribble penetration.”
A promising young center, an All-Star scoring wing and an interesting mix of guards isn’t an awful recipe, but the Blazers will need time to figure out the glaring logjam. Even more important, what version of Morant will Portland get? If the experiment crashes and burns, the Blazers will have his massive salary ($42 million and $44 million) on their books for two more seasons.
It just doesn’t seem like the Blazers have enough to keep up with the Western Conference powers or even the up-and-coming teams like the Jazz.
Offseason Recap
- Who’s in: Ja Morant, Branden Carlson, Jeremy Sochan, Micah Potter, Robert Williams III (re-signed)
- Who’s out: Jerami Grant, Kris Murray, Matisse Thybulle
Roster wise, the only considerable move the Blazers made over the offseason was the splashy trade for Morant. Since his value deteriorated in Memphis, Portland only had to give up Jerami Grant and Kris Murray (and no draft capital) to get the deal done. What the offseason did leave, though, is a lack of depth at forward. After Camara and Avdija, Portland doesn’t have any more true wings unless Jeremy Sochan makes the roster off his training camp deal. And that leaves much to be desired.
Maybe the Blazers trade Henderson for some help, but moving on from the No. 3 pick from three years ago for fill-in depth wouldn’t be great business. Camara certainly helps as a strong perimeter defender, but he can’t do it all by himself aside a lackluster defensive guard duo in Morant and Lillard. Holiday can help offset the defensive concerns, but he’s not getting any younger.
SI’s prediction for the 2026-27 Trail Blazers
The West will be a gauntlet—one the Blazers have too many questions to seriously compete in. Portland will likely hover around the play-in range once again, but the best case in that scenario is a likely series with the Thunder or the Spurs. And we saw how that worked out for the Blazers last year. More importantly, Portland’s year is about picking a direction moving forward.
PODCAST 🎧: Listen to SI’s NBA podcast, Open Floor, below or on Apple and Spotify. Watch the show on SI’s YouTube channel.
Blake Silverman is a writer at Sports Illustrated, primarily covering the NBA and WNBA. Before joining SI in November 2024 as a breaking/trending news writer, he covered the WNBA, NBA, G League and college basketball for numerous sites, including Winsidr, SB Nation and A10Talk. He’s an alum of both Michigan State and St. Bonaventure University, receiving a master’s degree from the Bonnies’ sports journalism program. Outside of work, he’s a husband, father, yogi and fairly mediocre tennis player who’s open to any tips on how to play defense in EA Sports College Football.
Follow blakesilverman

item.content:encoded:
The Moon is in Aquarius, and Dhanishtha Nakshatra adds to group influence, confidence, and movement. Friends or networks can help connect singles. Couples may focus more on shared goals and future experiences.
How to Navigate Today’s Energy
Keep love active, not too serious. Aquarius encourages independence, and Dhanishtha focuses on rhythm, movement and collective momentum. Couples may feel better doing things together instead of analysing each emotion separately. Singles should consider those who fit naturally into their social world. Stop chasing the attention of a flaky person. A relationship is healthier today when both partners bring energy, plans, and interest without trying to push intimacy.
Zodiac Signs That Need Care Today
Leo: You might want to set the emotional course of a relationship. Give the other person room to choose. If you control too much, motivation decreases.
Taurus: You could be annoyed by sudden changes to your plans. Don’t interpret flexibility as a lack of dependability. Maybe the person just doesn't want to be all regimented about spending time together.
Scorpio:
You might sense symptoms of protectiveness over a relationship that needs more time to mature.
Do not be a bystander to someone else’s decisions. Trust is built through repeated behaviour, not constant verification.
Cancer: You may feel less important due to group plans or social obligations. Do not compare private affection with public regard.
Zodiac Signs That May Enjoy Good Luck
Aquarius: Your social confidence can raise your profile. Singles may meet a prospective partner through online interactions, events, community circles or friends. Shared plans can energise existing relationships.
Gemini: Conversation can lead to an unlikely romantic opening.
Libra: Your social skills will be put to use. A nice invite or introduction might arouse interest. Couples can enjoy time with friends without losing their own time together.
Sagittarius: Spontaneous plans might just spice up the chemistry between a couple. Singles might meet someone motivated and full of energy. Couples will feel intimate when they do something new together.
Balanced Day for These Zodiac Signs
Aries:
Active attraction notwithstanding, mutual pacing matters more than speed.
Virgo: Your love life will blossom when you stop analysing every little sign of interest.
Capricorn: Emotional evolution continues when practical duties don’t occupy the whole day.
Pisces: Fun to socialise, but it may take longer for the deeper emotions to surface.
Lucky Action of the Day
Organise a collaborative activity that disrupts the status quo. A new environment or experience can lead to a more natural and effortless perception of attraction.

item.title: [gmenhq.com] Can Giants GM Joe Schoen survive a Jaxson Dart injury nightmare?
item.dc:creator: Lior Lampert
item.description: It might sound like hyperbole, but the fallout from losing Jaxson Dart has a franchise-altering trickle-down effect on the New York Giants. item.content:encoded:
It might sound like hyperbole, but the fallout from losing Jaxson Dart has a franchise-altering trickle-down effect on the New York Giants. Everyone is impacted by his suddenly bleak 2026 outlook, so why not start at the top with general manager Joe Schoen?
The Giants signed Schoen to a multi-year deal back in May, suggesting his job is safe — for now. But as former Baltimore Ravens head coach Brian Billick said, based on his own experience: "Signing a big contract extension doesn't mean you're going to be there, necessarily; it just means you're going to be paid."
For better or worse, the NFL is a results-driven business, and Schoen's track record precedes him in the worst way. New York is tied for the third-fewest wins in the league since he was hired in 2022 (23) and has posted three straight losing campaigns. His leash has been stretched surprisingly far, and expectations were raised with John Harbaugh's arrival, making Dart's availability (or lack thereof) a potential death knell.
How does Jaxson Dart's gutting injury affect Giants GM Joe Schoen?
Things have quickly gone from bad to worse to possibly catastrophic. Dart tried to reenter the game after getting hurt in the Giants' disastrous 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams. He was eventually ruled out for the night with what was initially believed to be an MCL sprain, which has devolved into a doomsday scenario.
If their showing against the Rams is any indication, New York is in trouble without Dart. The offense cratered following his departure from the contest, and the defense doesn't appear ready to pick up the slack. Put it all together, and Big Blue could be headed toward another lost season under Schoen.
Maneuvering for Dart (and star wide receiver Malik Nabers) has arguably been Schoen's biggest achievement with the G-Men. It's not easy to identify a game-changing talent at football's most important position. However, the football gods can taketh as easily as they giveth.
Does John Harbaugh lose patience?
Lest we forget, Schoen found himself on the losing end of a reported "power struggle" this offseason. He ceded the high ground in the Giants' new hierarchy centered around Harbaugh. In other words, the only reason the former wasn't only retained but also extended is that the latter OK'd the move.
Situations like this are fluid, though, and don't account for the absence of the club's most valuable player. The duo has gone on the record to let us all know that their working relationship is a collaborative effort and they're in sync. One wrong turn, especially involving Dart, may prompt Harbaugh to make changes, with moving on from Schoen being the easiest adjustment for the front office.
New York sinking sans Dart would be a massive indictment of the roster Schoen's had a hand in putting together. Of course, this squad has several Harbaugh recruits from his Baltimore days, yet there are 100 million reasons why he won't be the fall guy.

Community Bio Blitz
Saturday, Sept. 26, 10-11 a.m.
Eliza Howell Park, 23751 Fenkell Ave., Detroit
Join Sidewalk Detroit for a plant ID walk through Eliza Howell Park. Bring a cell phone with data, wear long pants and boots. Bug spray recommended.
Community Policy Fair
Saturday, Sept. 26, 11 a.m. to 2 p.m.
Wayne County Community College District, 801 W. Fort St., Detroit
Hopewell Church’s social justice ministry, Beyond 4 Walls, is connecting residents with policymakers, advocates, agency leaders and community organizations working in economic empowerment, housing, health and education. Because “policy is personal,” there will not be a traditional panel. Instead, residents will be able to engage directly, ask questions, connect with organizations and better understand how policy decisions show up in everyday life. Register now.
Expungement Fair
Saturday, Sept. 26, noon to 4 p.m.
Perfecting Church, 7616 E. Nevada Ave., Detroit
Learn more about clearing your criminal record, and apply to get started with the expungement process (which typically takes about eight months). Register now. Attorneys and law students can also apply to volunteer. 
Repair Cafe Volunteer Orientation
Saturday, Sept. 26, 1 to 4 p.m.
B. Nektar Meadery, 1511 Jarvis St., Ferndale
If you know how to sew or fix things — from clothes and jewelry to appliances and laptops — volunteer with the Repair Cafe! Their motto? “Let’s fix your stuff, together!” Pull up to learn how it works.
Detroit Solidarity Economy Assembly
Sunday, Sept. 27, 3-5 p.m.
General Baker Institute, 15798 Livernois Ave., Detroit
Members of co-ops, collectives, mutual aid groups and similar organizations are invited to build a vision for a collective economy. Learn more about the work already underway, and join for food, fellowship and future-building. RSVP now.
Black Reading Month Fireside Chat
Tuesday, Sept. 29, 6 p.m.
Howard Family Bookstore, 13803 Puritan St., Detroit
Close out Black Reading Month with one of its co-founders, Baba Malik Yakini, longtime Detroit institution builder and community organizer. Hosted by bookstore founder Jerjuan Howard. 
Documenters Speed Dating
Thursday, Oct. 1, 6-8 p.m.
Mockery Zero Proof, 7400 W. McNichols Road, Detroit
You don’t want to miss this! Detroit Documenters have teamed up with The Outlier Collective to bring together more than 16 local journalism leaders who will share insights on reporting, newsroom leadership, audience engagement, visual storytelling, technology and more. This event is designed for Documenters and Collective members, but it’s open to the public, and tickets are still available. Check out the lineup, and register now! 
Call for Student Artists
Apply by Friday, Oct. 2
Detroit’s Civil Rights, Inclusion and Opportunity Department wants student artists to submit work for the upcoming Civil Rights Summit. Art will be displayed all day for attendees to vote on. Artists can submit work in any medium on the theme of what civil rights looks and feels like in the 21st century. Get details, apply by Oct. 2, and attend the summit on Oct. 9. Email any questions to Naomi Barbour at naomi.barbour@detroitmi.gov. 
Open Call for Art
Feature your art at Paris Bar. Send a few photos of the artwork, a brief artist bio and short proposal to parisbarart@gmail.com. 
Call for Art
Get your art displayed for sale at Café Noir. Artists can submit up to two pieces of ready-to-hang artwork for sale between $100 and $500. No nudity, profanity or politically charged content. Get details and submit your work.
Destination: Liberation
Apply by Friday, Oct. 23
Detroit Heals Detroit is relaunching its 12-week travel immersion program for formerly incarcerated or justice-impacted youth. Ten people ages 18 to 25 have an opportunity to develop job readiness and community leadership skills. Get details and apply now. 
Now hiring
Communications and Design Coordinator
Detroit Disability Power is hiring a visual artist to expand its reach and create accessible graphics for social media, email, print and online spaces. The full-time position pays a salary of $55,000-$62,000 plus benefits. Learn more about the job requirements, desired skills and mindset. Then submit either a cover letter or audio or video recording, along with a résumé and portfolio. Apply by Sept. 23. 
Multiple Positions
Detroit Heals Detroit is hiring for several positions at The Healing Hub: Two part-time interns will help manage and evaluate activities and supervise youth participants. A part-time after-school program assistant will provide tutoring and homework help, and plan field trips and workshops, at $20 an hour. A Healing Hub director will work full time with unlimited days off for a salary of $45,000. Board members are being recruited too. All positions are hiring immediately. 
Paid Youth Internship
Detroit Area Youth Uniting Michigan (DAYUM) is seeking  interns. Those selected will meet one Sunday afternoon or weekday evening on Zoom, and attend three Saturday training sessions in November. Interns who complete all the trainings will receive a stipend of $400 at the end of November. Get details and apply by Oct. 14. 
MI Healthy Climate Fellow
Friends of Rouge Park is hiring someone to document and report on climate resilience benefits and ecosystem services in Detroit’s sprawling Rouge Park. The full-time position runs from January to August 2027, and pays $24 an hour, including benefits. You can learn more about MI Climate Fellows, get details on the position in Detroit, and apply by Oct. 6. 
Director of Foundation Services
Co.act Detroit is hiring someone to build and grow a portfolio of partners and philanthropists. The position pays a salary of $120,000 plus benefits. Get details and apply by Sept. 27. 
Major Gifts Officer
Focus: HOPE is hiring someone to solicit and steward donors supporting the organization’s mission. They will also lead volunteers and plan fundraising events. The full-time position pays a salary of $96,000 to $98,000. Those who require accommodations for the application, interview or job duties should email 725@focushope.edu. Apply now.
Seasonal Part-Time Bookseller
Next Chapter Books is looking for seasonal help. Must be a high school graduate who loves reading books, can lift at least 20 pounds, and work Saturdays. The position pays $16 an hour for 10-15 hours a week from mid-October through December. Get details and send a résumé to info@nextchapterbookstore.com to apply.
Operations Assistant
Inside Out Literary Arts is hiring a someone to manage the office, daily financial systems and events. The position pays between $20 and $25 for 10-15 hours a week. Get details on the job requirements, then submit your résumé and application by Oct. 18. Interviews will be in November, and the position is scheduled to start in January. 
Executive Director
The Michigan Environmental Justice Coalition is hiring someone to lead their strategic direction, raise funds and grow partnerships. The salary is $140,000-$150,000, plus benefits. Get details, and apply now. 
Multiple Positions
The Museum of Contemporary Art Detroit (MOCAD) is hiring a part-time social media and digital content manager to boost its digital presence. The position pays between $30 and $35 an hour. MOCAD is also hiring a full-time finance manager to oversee the museum’s budget, payroll and more at $65,000-$70,000 a year; and a full-time major gifts officer at a salary of $75,000-$85,000 to help grow philanthropic support. Learn more about each position. To apply, send your résumé and cover letter in a PDF file to jobs@mocadetroit.org. 
Human Resources Director
Local nonprofit health and wellness center American Indian Health and Family Services is hiring a full-time leader to ensure services are provided according to policy, procedure and standards. The HR director will earn full benefits and work in a new facility in Southwest Detroit. Learn more about the role and requirements, then apply. 
Community Engagement Liaison
O’Hair Park Community Association is hiring someone to engage residents, businesses, churches and schools to share resources and opportunities. Working hours are flexible for this part-time job that pays $20 an hour for up to 10 hours a week. Get details and apply by sending a résumé to Joyce Daniel at detjrm@aol.com. 
Community Captain
Rising Voices is hiring people to canvass neighborhoods and mobilize voters in Michigan’s Asian American communities and explain what’s on the ballot. The part-time, temporary position pays $25, starts this month and runs until the Nov. 3 election. Get details and apply now. 
Organizing Intern
Rising Voices is also hiring a recent graduate or undergraduate student for its internship. The intern will help coordinate grassroots-level efforts to build political power in local Asian American communities through monthly meetings, canvassing and issue-based campaigns. The internship is 15 hours a week from September to mid-December, and pays $17 an hour. Get details, then gather your résumé, interest letter, two writing samples and two references to apply. 
Electoral Canvasser
Detroit Action is hiring people to talk to residents about current issues and voter registration for November’s general election. Canvassers are paid $22 an hour. Learn more and apply now. 
Evergreen opportunities
Free Showers
Detroit Heals Detroit offers residents access to free, luxurious showers, complete with towels, body wash and more, plus a mini hygiene kit to go. Get clean every Monday from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. at The Healing Hub, 19510 Alcoy St., Detroit. 
Free Laundry Service
Detroit Heals Detroit offers residents access to a washer, dryer, detergent and laundry supplies in 90-minute slots every Wednesday from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. Sign up for an appointment starting at 11 a.m. on Mondays, and appointments are confirmed Tuesdays. Capacity is limited. 
Free Health Screenings
Wayne Health’s mobile units deliver health care and social services directly to neighborhoods and places of employment. Teams of registered nurses and other medical professionals offer screenings for things such as high blood pressure, diabetes, high cholesterol and kidney disease, as well as COVID-19 testing and vaccines. They can also connect you with mental health resources. To see when they’ll be in your neighborhood, view the event calendar. 
Free Tech Classes
Detroit Public Library offers a wide range of computer- and technology-related classes for all ages — from basic computer skills and troubleshooting your phone or internet to classes in productivity and graphic design software. Find free group and individual support at multiple library branches. 
Immigration Office Hours
Detroit People’s Assembly offers help with urgent immigration paperwork, including bond requests, stays of removal, temporary protected status filings and work permits. Office hours are 5-8 p.m. Thursdays at Grace in Action Church, 1725 Lawndale St., Detroit. 
Become an Immigration Court Observer
Take a self-paced course from the American Bar Association’s Commission on Immigration in preparation to volunteer as an immigration court observer. Learn firsthand about the immigration court system while helping identify patterns that will inform advocacy and support access to counsel and due process rights for noncitizens. Enroll now. 
Tell Your Story of Property Tax Foreclosure in Detroit
The Coalition for Property Tax Justice is collecting stories of Detroit property owners to build an archive of tax injustice. Have you experienced tax foreclosure? Share your story. 
Neighborhood Vitality Index Survey
Detroit adults can earn a $25 gift card by participating in an annual community-driven online survey about neighborhood improvements. The survey takes about 20 minutes to complete. 
Regional Freight Plan
Give feedback on the Southeast Michigan Council of Governments Regional Freight Plan draft policies and objectives. Take the survey. 
Education Survey
Education policy is a critical issue for Michigan’s next governor. Chalkbeat Detroit and the Detroit Free Press are teaming up to learn metro Detroiters’ priorities. Take the survey. 
Youth Engagement Survey
BridgeDetroit seeks to connect with local high school students ages 13-18 to understand how they consume news, what issues matter to them and how they want to engage civically. The survey will inform BridgeDetroit’s coverage and events. Learn more and take the survey. 
Detroit Wellbeing Survey
Be Well Beautiful People is leading a citywide effort to understand how residents feel about their well-being. The survey “will help shape future systems” that support collective well-being. Take the survey. 
We Walk Detroit
Join a walking group and exercise with friends you haven’t met yet. Through September, meet up for a one-hour walk at eight city parks, the Joe Louis Greenway and the riverfront. All participants get a T-shirt. Check out the schedule. 
Donate Furniture
The Furniture Bank of Metro Detroit needs donations of mattresses, sofas and other home goods in clean, working condition for families in need. Residents of Wayne, Oakland or Macomb counties can submit furniture donations online and schedule a free pickup. 
Volunteer With a Chess Club
The Wise Guys Chess Club is seeking volunteers to help with everything from coaching to youth mentoring, including graphic design, social media work and more. Sign up now to help empower the next generation of thinkers. 
Volunteer Usher
Detroit Public Theatre needs ushers this season. These volunteers can watch the shows they help with or get free tickets. Learn more and sign up now!

item.title: [BBC] 'Speed dating for trucks' saves money for food charity
item.dc:creator: Wendy Hurrell
item.description: - Published The food distribution charity Felix spent £5.6m last year collecting surplus produce, and getting it to the community organisations it supports. Richard Smith, director of food innovation at Felix, said: "These are costs we cannot cut. Without our logistics, this food would never reach the millions who need it most." But a new platform dubbed "speed dating for trucks" has been launched to reduce those costs. Using AI technology to bring together logistics providers, retailers and man
item.content:encoded:
- Published
The food distribution charity Felix spent £5.6m last year collecting surplus produce, and getting it to the community organisations it supports.
Richard Smith, director of food innovation at Felix, said: "These are costs we cannot cut. Without our logistics, this food would never reach the millions who need it most."
But a new platform dubbed "speed dating for trucks" has been launched to reduce those costs.
Using AI technology to bring together logistics providers, retailers and manufacturers, it matches spare haulage capacity with surplus food collections.
Early trials of the new software and system have already saved the charity money.
Smith added: "The benefits are all there - real and instant."
Deliveries of surplus food arrive all day at the Felix depot and kitchen in Poplar, east London.
It is sorted in the warehouse and redistributed to charities across London working to ease food poverty.
Until now, the administration has fallen to the logistics team at Felix (formerly the Felix Project), which books a haulier and pays for the transportation.
The costs soon add up.
Nicola Robinson, director of Alliance Food Sourcing (AFS) - a coalition of leading food companies - said: "Felix spent in 2025, £5.6m on 80,000 pallets, and three quarters of that cost was coming from third-party logistics companies.
"We thought we could take a look at that and if we tap into the spare capacity that we know exists within UK road hauliers, then we could put that to good use."
According to the Department for Transport, about 30% of all HGV journeys have spare capacity.
Using AI technology, the platform matches that space in lorries with deliveries to the Felix depots - hence the speed dating nickname.
Early trials with the food producer Greencore have led to a twice-weekly delivery of milk going to the Felix depot.
That route alone is projected to save the charity £20,000 a year.
Smith said: "The milk comes in every single week with very light touch from Felix, so we're barely getting involved.
"Now this is just a locked-in route, it happens every single week - that milk lands here and is back out to charities within 24 hours."
Currently, Greencore offers the service free of charge.
Darren Binns, head of logistics at Greencore, said: "There is an element of cost here but we think that we can absorb that cost, use the extra space that we have to do the right thing, to move surplus food into Felix's charity network."
Sainsbury's and logistics provider GXO have identified a further 10 routes for moving Felix food, with estimated annual savings of around £170,000.
Tesco, M&S and supply chain company Gist are also involved in the project, offering free consultancy and logistics support.
Data from the Trust for London showed that food insecurity has risen by 23% in London over the past two years.
Alongside the rise in need, transportation costs have gone up, and this is at a time when our changing climate sees demands that we reduce carbon emissions.
If the new platform is upscaled, AFS said it could save Felix £1m a year, as well as reduce road miles.
It said it would transform the way different sectors work, and urged more in the food industry to support the project.

Voters were able to meet 10 of the 12 candidates running for Idaho’s Legislature District 29 in Pocatello and District 28 representing Chubbuck and surrounding areas. item.content:encoded:
POCATELLO, Idaho (KIFI) – Pocatello spiced up the political scene with a non-partisan “Meet Your Candidates: Speed Dating-style” night at the Idaho State University ballroom tonight.
Voters were able to meet 10 of the 12 candidates running for Idaho’s Legislature District 29 in Pocatello and District 28 representing Chubbuck and surrounding areas.
The activity was sponsored by the Idaho State University Political Science Club, Southeast Idaho Citizens for Democracy and Braver Angels.
“We'd like to give the participants, the voters, an experience of meeting candidates up close and personal," said Braver Angels Organizer Dr. Michael Jindra.
Residents asked questions for 15 minutes to each of the five candidates running from their region. 
Voters inquired about data centers, healthcare, Medicare cuts, protecting public land, relations with the Shoshone-Bannock tribe and more.
"There's a lot of toxicity in politics right now through advertisements, through the internet," Jindra said. "This is a personal event that helps people get to know candidates face-to-face, and I think that kind of helps tone it down a little bit."
Candidates who participated are starred:
Idaho Senate District 28
*Jim Guthrie (R) and *Mandy Peace (D)
Idaho House of Representatives District 28 Seat A
*Kim Jackman (D) and Rick Cheatum (R) 
Idaho House of Representatives District 28 Seat B
*Dan Garner (R) and *Jayson Meline (D)
Idaho Senate District 28
*James Ruchti (D) and John Crowder (R)
Idaho House of Representatives District 29 Seat A
*Dustin Manwaring (R) and *Mary Shea (D)
Idaho House of Representatives District 29 Seat B
*Nate Roberts (D) and *Jennifer Miles (R)
Local News 8 will publish in-depth reports with each candidate in the weeks before the general election on November 3, 2026.

item.title: [thepostathens.com] Alexa Play: Dating apps are double-edged sword
item.dc:creator: Alexa Sanders
item.description: One of the worst sentences a girl’s friend group can hear is, “I downloaded Hinge again.” Generally, this can be excused following a breakup, but at its worst, it’s a woman defying her own logic and reasoning while crafting excuses for her horrible situationship “Because obviously, he’s super busy and nobody else understands.” Despite arguments that having a boyfriend is currently a social faux pas, people still seek connection. item.content:encoded:
One of the worst sentences a girl’s friend group can hear is, “I downloaded Hinge again.” Generally, this can be excused following a breakup, but at its worst, it’s a woman defying her own logic and reasoning while crafting excuses for her horrible situationship “Because obviously, he’s super busy and nobody else understands.”
Despite arguments that having a boyfriend is currently a social faux pas, people still seek connection. Additionally, straight women’s dating frustrations have generated numerous pop albums, and even their own term, heterofatalism. Heterofatalism, coined by Asa Seresin, a sexuality scholar, describes the phenomenon of straight women feeling embarrassed about their attraction toward men and desire to detach themselves from the world of dating and subsequent disappointment.
I don’t think the issue here is that men simply suck. Nor do I think the death of chivalry is entirely to blame. Dating apps may be part of the problem. With a large selection of profiles, dating app users are more likely to reject the profiles accessible to them. Women experiencing this rejection mindset are less likely to obtain matches. Despite access to more potential partners on dating apps, the act of choosing the right partner isn’t as clear.
Sam Kizer, assistant professor of instruction in sociology at Ohio University, recognizes the influence of assistive technology in modern dating. He discussed the various dating resources marketed towards single people, including cards to bring to a date encouraging face-to-face conversations, dating apps and generative artificial intelligence.
“The algorithm, the tech, the dating, the cards, the apps, the cards, whatever, they might be able to assist in finding people to evaluate,” Kizer said. “They themselves cannot be the evaluator.”
Although dating apps create an opportunity to meet new people and potentially introduce users to new labels or types of relationships, the mere act of creating a profile requires the user to exclude potential matches to some degree. On Hinge, if you say you’re looking for a long-term relationship, the algorithm within the app is already curating who is and isn’t available for you as a potential match.
Alongside dating app usage, increased AI use in daily life, from email writing to LinkedIn job searches, hinders their ability to make independent critical decisions. Effective communication skills are vital to healthy relationships; this becomes an issue with a growing number of people using generative AI chatbots to analyze and support their relationship decisions.
Generation Z has faced numerous barriers to healthy social development, leading to an increase in social anxiety and loneliness. Utilizing online spaces to meet people can mitigate potential fear of rejection, but these online connections are not likely to help people feel less lonely.
Dating is meant to feel good, and it’s not surprising even pop music artists are calling out when it doesn't. Human connection is messy, vulnerable and cannot be calculated by an app or algorithm. Even if you or your best friend resorts to redownloading dating apps once again, try to remember taking a risk against your typical standards or expectations might not be so risky.
Alexa Sanders is a senior studying psychology at Ohio University. Please note the opinions expressed in this column do not represent those of The Post. Want to talk to Alexa about her column? Email her at al683822@ohio.edu.

item.dc:creator: Kishori Sud
item.description: Your romantic strength comes from patience today. If emotions run high, avoid reacting immediately. Singles may attract someone through quiet confidence, while couples can deepen trust by handling a sensitive matter with understanding. item.content:encoded:
Your romantic strength comes from patience today. If emotions run high, avoid reacting immediately. Singles may attract someone through quiet confidence, while couples can deepen trust by handling a sensitive matter with understanding.
Love Horoscope Today for September 23, 2026: Avoid rushing to conclusions, but don't ignore inconsistencies either
Love Horoscope Today: Find daily astrological predictions for all sun signs.
Love Tip: Stay gentle without giving up your boundaries.
Crystal Remedy: Tiger Eye — carry it to encourage confidence, emotional balance, and calm responses.
You may want greater security in love, but don't let fear of losing someone make you overly protective. Singles should remain open to genuine connections, while couples can strengthen intimacy by creating a stronger sense of trust.
Love Tip: Security grows through trust, not control.
Crystal Remedy: Green Jade: Keep it near your bedside to encourage harmony, stability, and balanced affection.
You may realize that a romantic situation no longer fulfills you emotionally. Singles could feel ready to leave an old attachment behind, while couples may need to address whether both people are still moving in the same direction.
Love Tip: Walking away from what drains you can make space for healthier love.
Crystal Remedy: Aquamarine: Carry it during emotional transitions to encourage calm and clarity.
Someone may not be revealing their complete feelings or intentions. Avoid rushing to conclusions, but don't ignore inconsistencies either. Let actions give you the information you need.
Love Tip: Observe carefully before giving your trust completely.
Crystal Remedy: Black Tourmaline: Keep it close as a reminder to maintain healthy emotional boundaries.
Love may develop through consistency rather than grand gestures. Singles could notice someone dependable, while couples may strengthen their bond through practical support and keeping promises.
Love Tip: Pay attention to the person who shows up consistently.
Crystal Remedy: Bronzite: Carry it to encourage patience, reliability, and grounded emotional choices.
You may feel more selective about what you want from love. A direct conversation could clear up confusion or help you establish an important boundary. Singles may be drawn toward someone intelligent and straightforward.
Love Tip: Say what you mean without using distance as a defence.
Crystal Remedy: Sodalite: Keep it nearby during important conversations to encourage honest and clear communication.
You may be thinking seriously about the future of a connection. Singles could be deciding whether to explore something unfamiliar, while couples may discuss plans that require both people to look beyond the present.
Love Tip: Choose a direction based on your long-term values, not temporary uncertainty.
Crystal Remedy: Labradorite: Carry it when considering a new romantic direction to encourage perspective and adaptability.
A happy, stable energy surrounds your romantic life. Couples may enjoy quality time, a celebration, or a renewed sense of security. Singles could encounter someone through a social or familiar environment.
Love Tip: Let yourself enjoy a connection without searching for problems.
Crystal Remedy: Green Aventurine: Keep it nearby to encourage optimism, warmth, and harmonious connections.
Romantic tension may arise from competing expectations or opinions. Don't let a minor disagreement become a contest. Singles should also avoid getting drawn into complicated situations that bring more conflict than connection.
Love Tip: Protect the relationship from unnecessary competition.
Crystal Remedy: Red Jasper: Carry it to stay grounded and composed during emotionally charged conversations.
You may feel increasingly hopeful about your romantic future. A long term goal involving love could become clearer, whether that means commitment, meeting someone new, or deciding what kind of relationship you truly want.
Love Tip: Give your future enough attention to guide your present choices.
Crystal Remedy: Sunstone: Keep it close to encourage optimism, confidence, and positive romantic momentum.
A spontaneous romantic opportunity may appear. Singles could meet someone unexpectedly, while couples may benefit from breaking out of routine and doing something adventurous together.
Love Tip: Leave room for surprise without abandoning good judgment.
Crystal Remedy: Citrine: Carry it on social occasions to encourage confidence, openness, and joyful energy.
Your heart may feel ready for a fresh beginning. A new attraction, heartfelt conversation, or emotional breakthrough could bring renewed hope. Couples can deepen intimacy by expressing feelings openly.
Love Tip: Don't be afraid to receive the affection you've been hoping for.
Crystal Remedy: Rose Quartz: Keep it close to encourage tenderness, openness, and emotional connection.

Drake's goth girl, Pinkchyu, gave an interesting answer about her relationship with the rapper when asked where they stand today.
On Tuesday, Pinkchyu spoke to TMZ during a visit to Los Angeles. The influencer, who went viral for appearing on Drake's "20-v-1" speed dating stream, was mum when asked if she was "official" with the Canadian rapper.
As TMZ previously reported, Drake and Pinkchyu have hung out after the livestream ... and she even appeared in his new music video.
Pinkchyu is known for her eye-catching gothic look -- which has awarded her thousands of OnlyFans subscribers ... and even a mystery musician "barking" in her DMs.
Watch the clip where Pinkchyu also gave us an update on Drake buying her mom a home.

item.content:encoded:
Your Love Horoscope Is Here For Wednesday, September 23: Be Honest Today
Your zodiac sign's daily love horoscope is here for September 23, 2026. The Aquarius Moon trines Mercury in Libra on Wednesday, encouraging you to be completely honest.
While the Aquarius Moon inspires truth above all else, Mercury in Libra helps you express it in a way that benefits your relationship or dating life. This is not just about being honest with how you feel but choosing what is right for you instead of what you think you should be doing. Embrace authenticity so you can receive the love destined for you.
Love horoscopes for each zodiac sign on Wednesday, September 23, 2026:
Aries
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Say what actually matters, Aries. You deserve a full life, and on Wednesday, you may need to discuss with your partner what that actually means.
You don’t need to spend all your time together, but you do need to communicate how you’re actually feeling. Create space not just for love, but for friends and family. This is about creating a relationship that supports the life you want to live.
Taurus
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Be honest about what you can give, Taurus. Wednesday is all about truth, and for you, that means owning what you can actually give a relationship right now.
It’s better to own the reality of your current situation than pretend it doesn’t exist. You may be preoccupied with family matters or with furthering your career. You can have a healthy relationship through this period, but you first must be honest about how much you actually have to give.
Gemini
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Don’t be afraid to speak your truth, Gemini. You are about to make an important decision in your life. This could lead to commitment or marriage with the person you love, but remember that you have a say in what that looks like.
Your partner may be more of a traditionalist, but you are finding yourself drawn to the unconventional. On Wednesday, be honest about the kind of commitment you want and what a marriage based in your truth would actually look like.
Cancer
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
This can work out, Cancer, but you must change your perspective toward the connection in your life. On Wednesday, you are urged to challenge the blueprint you’ve been given for love. Just because you followed a specific formula before doesn’t mean you are meant to now.
Honor your authentic desires for love, even if that means maintaining greater independence. Your relationship may not look how you expected, but that's OK.
Leo
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Honor your feelings, but be open to discussing them, Leo. September 23 brings about an important conversation in your romantic life. Be honest with your partner about your feelings and hold space for their thoughts too.
On Wednesday, talk about your future. A relationship isn’t solely based on feelings but on how you can build a life together. That is what you are meant to focus on now.
Virgo
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Decide what matters most, Virgo. Focus on what you deserve in relationships, but also make sure you're not giving more than you’re receiving.
Wednesday's energy helps you understand what you need in your life so you can make sure you recieve it. You must figure this out on your own before having a conversation with your partner. Otherwise, you may get talked into accepting less.
Libra
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Do what feels good to your soul, Libra. While this is only the start of your zodiac season, the universe is wasting no time bringing divine occurrences into your romantic life.
On Wednesday, speak up about what and who you truly want. With the Aquarius Moon, you are thinking about commitment; however, it will look different than the relationships in your past. Don’t just go with the flow, but honor what feels meant for you.
Scorpio
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
You sometimes get caught up in your head, Scorpio, worrying about what you should say or how honest you should be. On Wednesday, let go of this pressure. You don't need to express yourself perfectly or decide the rest of your life this very second.
You are in a phase of freedom and learning what is authentic for you. While you should say yes to new opportunities, you don't need to commit to any one path. Your future is changing more rapidly than you know.
Sagittarius
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Reach out to a trusted friend on Wednesday, Sagittarius. You are trying to figure out what to do with a new emotional truth. This could relate to someone new in your life or the sudden realization that you are in love.
Whatever it is, talk through it with a trusted friend before taking action. Just be sure the person you talk to truly has your best interests at heart, and not their own agenda.
Capricorn
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
You can’t quantify love, Capricorn. No matter how hard you try to make logical decisions or guarantee success in your romantic life, that's just not possible. Instead, you must put in the work and learn to communicate better and trust your instincts.
On Wednesday, you may need to have an uncomfortable conversation. It won't be easy, but it will bring greater clarity moving forward. Hold space for the process instead of rushing to a conclusion.
Aquarius
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Listen to your heart, Aquarius. There will always be external noise and people with loud opinions about what you should do. However, you must tune all that out.
On Wednesday, you are on the verge of a beautiful new chapter in your romantic life, but you must listen to your heart to fully embrace it. Practice slowing your mind down and focusing on your breathing, as you need to be in a calm place to truly make your own decisions.
Pisces
Photos: NASA & sparklestroke | Design: YourTango
Let them in, Pisces. Someone in your life wants to know the real you. The only issue is that you’ve gotten so used to keeping everything to yourself that it is difficult to open up. It’s not that you don’t trust them, but when left to your own devices, you develop a strong inner world.
Yet, love means letting someone in, even if you’re not sure how. On Wednesday, say more instead of less. Don’t be afraid to show this special person the unique way you see the world.
Kate Rose is a writer, spiritual astrologist, relationship and life intuitive counselor, and bespoke retreat curator.

item.content:encoded:
Christina Haack has received another chance at love with Christopher Larocca.
After the pair were spotted on a joint trip to Italy in October 2024 followed by an appearance at Amy Sexton’s holiday party in Laguna Beach, California, in December 2024, Us confirmed in January 2025 that Haack was dating Larocca.
The couple went Instagram official in February 2025, going on to make their red carpet debut in May 2025.
Haack recently went through a public divorce from Hall in July 2024 after over two years of marriage.
“Everyone’s just doing better since he’s gone. Just all that negative energy,” she said during an episode of Christina on the Coast, referring to her children Taylor and Brayden whom she shares with ex Tarek El Moussa and son Hudson whom she shares with ex Ant Anstead. “I truly tried to make that work.”
Keep scrolling to learn more about Haack and Larocca’s relationship:
October 2024
The Daily Mail claimed that Haack and Hall were seen on a trip to Italy together.
December 2024
The pair were spotted at Sexton’s holiday party in Laguna Beach, per Daily Mail.
January 2025
Us confirmed that Haack was dating Larocca, who is the CEO of Network Connex in Orange County, California. Later that month, the couple were spotted at LAX traveling to Paris for Haack’s business trip.
February 2025
Haack and Larocca went Instagram official when she shared a photo of the pair flying on a private plane.
“Some plane flights must be hard,” she captioned the post.
That same month, Haack and Larocca went on a double date with Tarek and his wife, Heather Rae El Moussa.
“First round of interviews ✅,” Tarek shared in an Instagram post.
March 2025
Larocca appeared in the background of The Flip Off’s season finale.
April 2025
Haack shared in an Instagram post about anxious attachment that finding a man “who has his own amazing career, life & hobbies (who also happens to have zero jealousy) can at times feel strange for someone who has had the opposite.”
Later that month, Haack’s ex Tarek told Us that the “double dates” with Larocca and Haack are “actually fun.”
“The new guy she’s dating, I really like him. He’s really nice,” he shared. “Honestly, he just seems like a good guy. She’s going through a really tough situation and, based on my conversations with her, he’s supportive, he’s guiding, he’s experienced and he is giving her good advice.”
May 2025
The couple made their red carpet debut at The Flip Off For Your Consideration Emmy event in Los Angeles.
“A supportive partner > everything,” Haack shared via her Instagram Story.
September 2026
To mark two years of dating, Haack shared a heartfelt appreciation post for Larocca.
“Two years of getting to know you. Together we built a champagne brand from the ground up, partnered on a flip for tv (coming soon) and traveled to amazing places,” she wrote via Instagram on September 21. “I have watched you handle everything with grace and understanding and therefore you have taught me to do the same. Thank you for making my life EASY. What a true gift that is. A gift I would not have appreciated in my younger years. Taking things slow and not rushing through life is something I also can greatly appreciate in my 40s. Thank you for being a true partner in all the ways @cml949 🤍.”

item.dc:creator: Anna Iovine
item.description: The rising cost of living has impacted singles for years now, and a new report from payment service Zelle shares new insights on just how much their bank accounts influence how (and if) they find love. Zelle's Economics of Dating Report found that the vast majority (84 percent) of Gen Z and millennial daters say rising cost has affected their dating lives (according to an Aug. 2026 national survey of 1,800 Gen Z and millennial adults who've dated within the past year). item.content:encoded:
The rising cost of living has impacted singles for years now, and a new report from payment service Zelle shares new insights on just how much their bank accounts influence how (and if) they find love.
Zelle's Economics of Dating Report found that the vast majority (84 percent) of Gen Z and millennial daters say rising cost has affected their dating lives (according to an Aug. 2026 national survey of 1,800 Gen Z and millennial adults who've dated within the past year).
Around a third (32 percent) said they're going on fewer dates, and one in 10 (11 percent) have stopped dating because they can't afford it.
You May Also Like
AdultFriendFinder — readers’ pick for casual connections
Tinder — top pick for finding hookups
Hinge — popular choice for regular meetups
As Mashable reported this year, socioeconomic factors can definitely hinder dating. Not only can some young people not afford dates, but more are living at home and can't buy a home. This can then delay when people get married and have children.
But for those young adults still in the dating pool, Zelle's report found that some respondents are choosing less expensive activities (40 percent), preferring more frequent economical dates to occasional expensive ones (38 percent), and suggesting free activities (37 percent).
And in this economy, being seen as frugal is a good thing. Thirty-eight percent said they judged someone positively for planning an affordable, thoughtful date — more than the 23 percent who said the same for someone who put together an extravagant, high-end one.
Other financial green flags include being thoughtful with money (56 percent), being honest and transparent about money (54 percent), planning a thoughtful, budget-friendly date (52 percent), and paying without making the situation awkward (52 percent).
On the flipside, there are some red flags when it comes to money and dating, such as making someone uncomfortable about what they can afford, expecting the other person to pay for everything, complaining about every price, and talking too much about income — all of which 47 percent of participants said gave them the ick. Around the same amount, 46 percent, also flagged making a big deal about paying.
Money anxiety abounds these days, including when trying to find a partner. Among women respondents, being rejected and spending too much ranked equally as sources of dating anxiety (37 percent). Other sources of anxiety are spending too much on a date (34 percent of participants said this), making sure a date fits within their budget (29 percent), discussing finances (28 percent), and asking who pays (25 percent).
Twenty-six percent said they won't bring up payment with their date at all.
This all seems like glum news, but at least 89 percent of daters are still putting themselves out there. There are dating apps you can use for free and low-cost outings, too, like a walk in the park. Otherwise, some singles might find themselves turning to AI for a cheaper date.
Anna Iovine is the associate editor of features at Mashable. Previously, as the sex and relationships reporter, she covered topics ranging from dating apps to pelvic pain. Before Mashable, Anna was a social editor at VICE and freelanced for publications such as Slate and the Columbia Journalism Review. Follow her on Instagram.

The Love Horoscope Predictions for September 23, 2026
, bring a reflective, watchful mood to relationships. The Moon is in Aquarius; Shravana Nakshatra heightens the value of listening, understanding, and the unspoken. Today couples can recognise key emotional cues. A conversation can yield a single useful piece of information.
How to Navigate Today’s Energy
Watch the tone, watch the timing, watch the behaviour repeated. Aquarius can hide emotions. Shravana is learning by listening with the intent to understand. Partners may convey more through informal comments than explicit statements. Let the conversation flow. Singles should not feel they have to impress. Simply asking the right question can create a greater sense of intimacy than talking incessantly. If something is unclear, ask for context before forming an opinion.
Zodiac Signs That Need Care Today
Leo: You might want a more overt display of affection, but the other person may be more reserved than you thought. Instead of seeking attention, see if they are showing interest in less obvious ways.

Sagittarius: You may discover that a stimulating conversation can result in a deeper attraction. Singles can meet a potential partner through networking, learning, travel or a group setting.

Feelings can develop slowly and steadily if expectations are realistic and communication is simple.

item.title: [cosmopolitan.com] Looking for Love Online? These Are the Safest Dating Apps to Try
item.dc:creator: Syeda Khaula Saad
item.description: Dating apps don’t exactly have the best rep right now. Apps have seen a drop in users and just this month TIME declared that they are dead. Everyone has their own guess as to why swiping feels slightly cringe: People want to make in-person connections, they think everyone on the apps is ugly, and, importantly users—mostly women—just don’t feel safe. item.content:encoded:
Dating apps don’t exactly have the best rep right now. Apps have seen a drop in users and just this month TIME declared that they are dead.
Everyone has their own guess as to why swiping feels slightly cringe: People want to make in-person connections, they think everyone on the apps is ugly, and, importantly users—mostly women—just don’t feel safe.
While I am a dating app retiree, I still vividly remember the amount of unhinged and frankly, frightening messages I received from men while on the apps. I know girlfriends who have been catfished, threatened, and even borderline stalked by men they swiped right on (and even ones they didn’t).
The people behind the apps are aware of the safety concerns and some (not all) have taken real steps to make sure their users feel as comfortable as possible—because trying to find love online is already difficult enough without having to worry about some creep using AI photos to trick you into meeting up.
So if you’re looking to swipe without worrying about your safety, here are some of the safest dating apps out there. Unfortunately, you’re on your own when it comes to what your matches look like.
Bumble
Despite the fact that I would never message a man first, Bumble is really steps ahead of a lot of other dating apps. They have one of the most extensive set of user-facing safety tools out there: photo verification, optional ID verification, and in-app voice and video calls. It also has the Share Date feature, which lets you share the details of an upcoming date with a trusted friend or family member. Plus, it blurs out potentially explicit photos, allows you to block, report, and unmatch someone, and even has a Deception Detector for users that are flagged as potential fake or scam accounts. It really gives you a lot of ways to vet someone before ever handing over your number.
Tinder
Tinder’s reputation has come a long way. What used to be known as “the hookup app” is now a pretty decent place to get to know someone—all while staying safe.
The app requires a Face Check, photo verification, Share My Date (similar to Bumble), and of course the ability to block and report someone. What really makes it a great option is the fact that users are prompted with “Are You Sure?” and “Does This Bother You?” message interventions to prompt people to think before they send something inappropriate, as well as the chance to report if something crosses the line.
Hinge
Hinge has become a lot more aggressive lately when it comes to authenticating its users. Its Face Check includes a video selfie and liveness check, which is then compared to profile photos. This can help detect duplicate or scam accounts.
Hinge’s Help Center also includes a variety of articles on “Safe Dating,” including pieces on consent, boundaries, and how to protect yourself from scammers.
Coffee Meets Bagel
Coffee Meet Bagel has always been known as a dating app for people who are really intentional about dating. And now, it has a bunch of safety features to make that more possible. The app has a live selfie verification—which has been completed by 70 percent of its users.
Match
Match focuses on moderation and user safety. Like some of the other apps on this list, it offers blocking, human moderation, anti-harassment measures, and privacy controls that lets users set who can contact them and what info goes on their profile. The app also gives users the chance to flag specifically for fake profiles, requests for money, and other violations.

item.dc:creator: Eric W Dolan
item.description: A recent study suggests that a woman’s level of religious belief influences how she evaluates potential partners on swipe-based dating apps like Tinder. When navigating these platforms, women often face a trade-off between evaluating a potential partner’s genetic fitness and their willingness to invest in a relationship. item.content:encoded:
A recent study suggests that a woman’s level of religious belief influences how she evaluates potential partners on swipe-based dating apps like Tinder. When navigating these platforms, women often face a trade-off between evaluating a potential partner’s genetic fitness and their willingness to invest in a relationship. The findings indicate that more religious women show a broader initial receptivity to men’s profiles, while overall, women tend to prefer softer facial features but surprisingly favor exaggerated, unverifiable profile biographies. The research was published in Psychology & Sexuality.
Swipe-based dating applications require users to make split-second decisions about potential partners based on a single photograph and a brief biography. These platforms compress mate selection into rapid, low-consequence choices, forcing users to rely heavily on highly visible cues. When evaluating a photograph, people often pick up on facial sexual dimorphism, which refers to how physically masculinized or feminized a face appears.
Earlier research discovered that women often prefer softer, feminized male faces over hyper-masculine ones. For instance, a 1998 study showed that women routinely find feminized male faces more attractive than strictly masculine alternatives. This preference exists partly because rugged features are linked to lower trustworthiness, with a 2012 study indicating that women view more masculine men as more likely to engage in unfaithful behavior.
Religious norms often emphasize long-term relational stability and sexual restraint. Supporting this, a study covered by PsyPost in 2017 indicated that higher religious commitment is associated with a greater preference for long-term mating strategies and fewer sexual partners. Because of this association, researchers expected that religious women might be more cautious when evaluating potential partners online.
The new study builds on this concept by examining how initial visual judgments interact with written profile details and a woman’s own religiosity on modern dating apps. The research was conducted by Katherine L. Sheetz, a Ph.D. candidate, and Lisa L. M. Welling, a professor of psychology, both at Oakland University.
“Online dating has changed the way people make initial judgments about potential partners, especially since the COVID-19 pandemic forced the majority of dating online,” Welling, who directs the Welling Research Lab, told PsyPost. “Swipe-based platforms reduce initial mate choice selections to very rapid decisions based on relatively limited visual and textual information, yet we know relatively little about how individual differences, such as religiosity, shape those early decisions.”
“With this study, we were particularly interested in religiosity because it is associated with sexual restraint, restricted sociosexuality (meaning lower openness to casual sex), and long-term relationship motivations on average,” Welling explained. “We therefore wanted to test whether more religious women would be more selective when evaluating potential male partners in an online context, particularly when profiles contained cues that could be relevant to apparent trustworthiness and relationship intentions.”
The study included 439 single cisgender women between the ages of 18 and 38 who were primarily attracted to men. The participants completed an online survey that began with questionnaires assessing their religious beliefs and their motivations for using dating applications. Afterward, they completed a simulated Tinder task where they viewed 20 distinct male dating profiles. Each profile featured a photograph of a smiling man and a short, 500-character biography.
The researchers manipulated the photographs using computer software so that the faces appeared either 50 percent more masculinized or 50 percent more feminized, while keeping skin tone and identity the same. The profile biographies were also written to be either trustworthy or untrustworthy.
Trustworthy biographies included verifiable, specific information regarding education or employment and avoided grand claims. Untrustworthy biographies featured exaggerated personal achievements and vague job descriptions, a tactic known as selective self-presentation. The participants had to either accept each profile, mimicking a right swipe, or reject the profile, mimicking a left swipe.
The researchers found that facial features strongly guided the women’s choices. Profiles featuring masculinized faces had approximately 56 percent lower odds of being accepted compared to profiles with feminized faces. However, the biographic text yielded unexpected results. Instead of favoring honest profiles, women showed a preference for the exaggerated text. Profiles with untrustworthy biographies had about 24 percent higher odds of acceptance compared to those with straightforward, trustworthy biographies.
“We were also surprised that profiles containing our ‘untrustworthy’ biographies were accepted more often than profiles containing the ‘trustworthy’ biographies,” Welling said. “The manipulation successfully changed perceptions of trustworthiness in the intended direction, so the finding suggests that participants may have been responding to other characteristics conveyed by those biographies, rather than simply preferring less trustworthy partners. We think it might have been something like perceived confidence in the untrustworthy bios because they tended to be more boastful.”
A woman’s level of religious belief also played a role in her swiping behavior, but not in the direction the researchers originally predicted. Higher religiosity predicted higher overall profile acceptance across the board. For each one-unit increase on the study’s seven-point religiosity scale, the odds of a profile being accepted increased by roughly 38 percent.
“The main takeaway is that religiosity was associated with greater initial receptivity to potential partners in our simulated online-dating task, rather than greater selectivity, which is the opposite of what we originally predicted,” Welling noted.
She cautioned that while the association was statistically reliable, it was not necessarily a massive shift in real-world behavior. “An odds ratio is not the same thing as saying that someone was 30% or 38% more likely to date someone,” Welling clarified. “The outcome in our study was simply whether a participant accepted a profile in a controlled, simulated swiping task. In other words, our findings suggest that religious women are more likely to be open to dating men with a greater range of characteristics, but not that they necessarily would accept more men after that initial swipe.”
In exploratory analyses, the researchers looked at why the women used dating apps in the first place. Women who used the apps with the goal of finding a relationship accepted fewer profiles overall, showing a 38 percent reduction in acceptance odds for each one-unit increase in relational motivation. Entertainment or exploratory motives for using the app had no statistical effect on acceptance rates.
The preference for exaggerated biographies is in tension with research covered by PsyPost in 2016, which found that dating profiles featuring heavy bragging reduced viewers’ intentions to contact the owner. This difference might be explained by how the new study was designed, as the simulated Tinder task measured immediate profile acceptance during rapid swiping rather than a deliberate intention to date the profile owner.
As with all research, there are a few things to keep in mind. The simulated paradigm was not a fully interactive dating application, meaning real-world swiping behavior might differ. The acceptance of a profile in this specific task might reflect a general openness to new experiences or basic social interaction, rather than true romantic intent.
“The biggest caveat is that accepting a dating profile is not the same thing as choosing a partner, having sex with someone, entering a relationship, or taking a real-world interpersonal risk,” Welling emphasized. “Our measure captured an early-stage decision about whether a profile was sufficiently appealing to remain in consideration for potential further contact.”
She also warned against misinterpreting the biography finding as evidence that women prefer dishonest men. “Our biographies combined different aspects of self-presentation, including the extent to which information could theoretically be externally verified and the degree of selective self-presentation,” Welling explained. “Although they produced the intended differences in perceived trustworthiness, they may also have conveyed other characteristics, such as confidence… or like social status, that then influenced profile acceptance.”
The religiosity measure used in the study combined social elements, like attending religious services, with intrinsic elements, like personal beliefs. Social religiosity is often linked to higher interpersonal trust, which might explain the unexpectedly high acceptance rates among religious women. The study sample was also limited to young college-aged women in the United States, meaning the results might not automatically apply to other demographics.
Future research could use eye-tracking technology to see exactly which parts of a dating profile women pay the most attention to. Researchers might also separate different types of religious belief to better understand how they affect romantic risk-taking online. This would provide a better picture of how individuals navigate trust and uncertainty in the digital dating world.
“A major next step is to make the dating environment more realistic and to see how these findings translate into the in-person dating world,” Welling told PsyPost. “Our task captured the rapid decision-making aspect of swipe-based dating similar to dating apps like Tinder, but it was still a controlled simulation and results from face-to-face dating may differ.”
“I think the broader point is that online dating is an interesting setting for studying human decision-making because it makes the initial stages of mate evaluation unusually visible,” Welling concluded. “People are making rapid judgments from photographs, short biographies, and other limited cues, and those judgments reflect both characteristics of the profile and characteristics of the person doing the judging. Our findings suggest that we should be cautious about assuming that a characteristic associated with one aspect of mating psychology will necessarily predict behavior in another context.”
The study, “Holy swipes: the influence of religiosity on mate choice in online dating,” was authored by Katherine L. Sheetz and Lisa L. M. Welling.
