item.content:encoded:
UPWARD RELAUNCHES AS THE HOME OF MODERN COURTSHIP
With 72% of Gen Z wanting to get married,



Launched in 2020, Upward was built from a community that had strong conviction around faith, family and marriage. The relaunch builds on that foundation to welcome a broader generation reclaiming traditional courtship for modern life, where wanting a family is an ambition to embrace, not something to downplay.
"For a generation told to keep things casual and see where they go, saying you want marriage can almost feel countercultural," said

The relaunch brings modern courtship to life through a refreshed app experience designed to make values, future goals and relationship expectations more visible earlier in dating.
- Chivalry Mode is an opt-in experience for members who prefer a more traditional first-move dynamic. When both members opt in, he is encouraged to send the first message and she chooses whether to respond or politely unmatch.
- Marriage Timeline lets members share when they hope to get married and see whether potential matches share a similar timeline.
- Core Values gives members a way to show what matters most to them and quickly see whether they share a potential match's priorities.
This is modern courtship in action: women are clear about their standards, men pursue with purpose, and both move toward marriage together.
The clearest proof of Upward's purpose is why members join and why they leave. Nearly every Upward member ages 18–30 surveyed says they want a family, making "family" the platform's most-selected Core Value. And the #1 reason members say they leave is the outcome Upward is built for: they found someone worth leaving the app for.
The relaunch also introduces a new visual identity created in partnership with Corner Table Creative. A refined logo and app icon, distinctive typography and romantic imagery give Upward a bolder, more confident expression of its marriage-minded purpose. Drawing from Americana and the intimacy of a personal scrapbook, the new identity feels warm, nostalgic and distinctly human, anchored by subtle ring-inspired detail.
The accompanying "Wanted for Life" campaign brings that purpose to life through a playful, modern take on wanted posters. It celebrates the qualities members want in a lifelong partner, from good manners and meaningful effort to commitment that goes the distance. Through playful lines like "Known to change a tire, not his feelings for you" and "Often described as wifey material," Upward puts commitment and courtship where its members believe they belong: at the center of dating, not in a conversation saved for later.
"We wanted Upward's new brand to feel as intentional as the people who use it," said
The campaign will roll out across paid and organic social, streaming video and audio ads, with additional creative featuring real Upward couples who found lasting love on the app, bringing modern courtship to life from first match to marriage.
About Upward
Upward is the home of modern courtship, built for people who know marriage is the goal and believe the way they date should reflect it. Part of
About Match Group
Match Group (NASDAQ: MTCH), through its portfolio companies, is a leading provider of digital technologies designed to help people make meaningful connections. Our global portfolio of brands includes Tinder®, Hinge®, Upward®, Match®, Meetic®, OkCupid®, Pairs™, PlentyOfFish®, Azar®, BLK®, and more, each built to increase our users' likelihood of connecting with others. Through our trusted brands, we provide tailored services to meet the varying preferences of our users. Our services are available in over 40 languages to our users all over the world.

item.content:encoded:
Si de promesas de la música pop estamos hablando, sin duda tenemos que meter en la conversación a Freya Skye. Esta joven artista -de apenas 16 años- se está posicionando como una de esas chicas con un sueño musical que acaban convirtiéndose en grandes estrellas; y es que a su corta edad -y tras participar en Eurovisión Junior y protagonizar las películas de Zombies en Disney Channel-, la de Reino Unido está más que decidida a disparar su carrera en la industria.

Ya durante este 2026, Freya nos ha conquistado con el lanzamiento de su primer EP, stardust. De la mano de seis canciones llenas de energía pop y dominadas por su increíble capacidad vocal, la artista ha empezado a introducirnos su universo sonoro, y hacia dónde quiere dirigir su recorrido musical. Así, tras la llegada de canciones como silent treatment o petty –con las que suma millones de escuchas-, Freya ha querido dar un paso más.

Dos meses antes de aterrizar su gira mundial en España -y sí, a sus 16 años está en medio de la gira Stars Align que pisará Australia, Estados Unidos, Europa, Latinoamérica y Asia-, la de Buckinghamshire nos ha dado una sorpresa que narra a la perfección algo que les puede pasar a todos los jóvenes del mundo: tener mal gusto a la hora de 'elegir' a una persona con la que estar. Bad Taste aterrizó la semana pasada en plataformas digitales; y ha tenido tal éxito en las listas, que deja claro una vez más que Freya es una de las próximas estrellas pop.

LOS40

LOS40

El 'Bad Taste' de Freya Skye

En medio de su gira mundial Stars Align –y como parece que no podía estarse quieta sin seguir dejando su creatividad musical desarrollarse y fluir-, Freya Skye ha decidido regalarnos una novedad musical de lo más reveladora. La británica lanzó el pasado viernes 18 de septiembre bad taste, un tema pop desenfadado que podría convertirse en el himno de cualquier adolescente frustrada por las personas de las se enamora.

Aunque no se trata de una canción que vaya a formar parte de su álbum debut -según informó la artista al medio Billboard-, sí que espera que pueda ir preparando a sus seguidores y "entusiasmarles" por su próxima etapa en la industria musical. Y de hecho, en un fin de semana marcado por el lanzamiento de canciones como new trick de ROSÉ o el nuevo álbum de Miley Cyrus, ha sido bad taste la canción votada por los seguidores del medio estadounidense como su favorita –con un 82% de los votos-.

'Stars Align Tour'

Después de protagonizar dos películas de la saga Zombies de Disney Channel junto a otra de las grandes promesas de la industria tanto musical como cinematográfica, Malachi Barton, Freya Skye ha decidido centrarse durante un tiempo en su carrera en solitario. Y lanzarse a los escenarios con una gira mundial, Stars Align Tour.

Este tour comenzó en Australia el pasado 7 de junio, y pisará Estados Unidos y varios países europeos antes de aterrizar en España -con LOS40 como emisora oficial- el próximo 27 de noviembre. Freya Skye actuará en Madrid, en Live Las Ventas, y cerrará esta gran gira mundial de Stars Align con esta fecha en la capital española. Después, se adentrará en la parte del tour que corresponde a Latinoamérica -ya el próximo 2027-, con una serie de fechas que ha anunciado recientemente en sus redes sociales.

Letra de 'bad taste'

Si quieres unirte al universo sonoro de Freya Skye antes de su concierto en Madrid, aquí tienes la letra completa de bad taste:

At this point, it's just common sense

All that noise, that’s just evidence

I love a good messy situation

Yeah, you know me and I'm not complainin'

You call it problematic

I call it gotta have it

I like a boy with baggage

I got bad taste

But you sure know how to make my heart race

You’ve been livin' rent-free, chillin' in the backseat of my brain

It's a good start, you look like a good heartbreak

Guess I got, I got bad taste

item.title: [The Age] My generation has lost the ability to date in real life. Dating apps aren’t helping
item.dc:creator: Saria Ratnam
item.description: My dating app experiences haven’t been great. There have been ghosters and time-wasters and people who seemed fun over text but couldn’t hold a conversation in person. item.content:encoded:
My dating app experiences haven’t been great. There have been ghosters and time-wasters and people who seemed fun over text but couldn’t hold a conversation in person.
My friends, though, have had some real Hinge horror stories.
One went on a date with a guy who told her he was planning to write his PhD thesis on “the philosophy of woman” but somehow didn’t notice that he had been explaining it for 30 minutes without letting the woman across from him speak.
Another girl went on a date with someone who made her do their laundry, and pay for it. They claimed they had a new debit card that didn’t work and hadn’t been able to do their laundry for two weeks as a result.
And one friend experienced “Hinge-cest”, where she and all her friends had ended up dating the same men. There are “Hinge celebrities” who have gone on so many dates that their reputation precedes them.
Sounds like the ideal environment for meeting the love of your life, right?
Despite the technology’s poor reputation, it feels like everyone my age is on the apps. However, I only know a handful who have actually ended up in relationships with people they met online. Most, after weeks or months of scrolling, texting and going on dates, become frustrated and delete the app. And then, after failing to meet someone in real life, they re-download it.
So why are so many young people using dating apps if they don’t work? I believe it’s because my generation doesn’t know how to date in person.
Gen Z spent some of its formative dating and socialising years in lockdown, and we’ve grown up communicating over the internet. So it makes sense that this has had a lingering effect.
Dating apps seem to offer an easy way out. I do find it easier to speak to a new person online; shyness and awkwardness don’t come across over text. And perhaps most importantly, online rejection is far less humiliating.
But our dependence on dating apps might be making dating harder for us.
The idea that everyone is on Hinge has made making a move in person a completely foreign idea. Gen Z has lost the willingness to take a chance and just ask someone out, which dating has always relied on.
The gamification of dating makes us view it as a lazy activity – something we can do without leaving our bedrooms.
What’s worse is the horrible culture fostered by these apps. Ghosting people and talking to more than 10 people at once are considered normal. It’s no wonder users seem to forget they’re interacting with real humans. Similarly, your entire judgment of someone is based on a few photos.
None of this is conducive to genuine connection. It’s a tick-box model of dating, where you reject anyone who doesn’t fit your “ideal partner” criteria based on their photo and a few titbits of information. All this does is teach us to how to market ourselves to please other people and relentlessly judge others.
Dating in real life can be the opposite: you might end up with someone who doesn’t tick all the boxes you thought you wanted, but who ticks others that you didn’t realise you needed. The most important things, like real-life chemistry, communication style and personality, can’t be captured in a dating-app profile.
Although dating apps can have value for those who don’t have many opportunities to meet new people in real life, we need to break away from the mindset that they’re the only way to connect.
After the end of my last relationship, a friend told me to “keep going out, meeting new people, and something would happen eventually”. So, I made a conscious effort to say yes to every invitation that came my way – whether it was a spontaneous dinner, a side-quest that sends the night in a new direction, or a new book club. Even when I felt busy, or tired, or didn’t think I’d enjoy it.
And my life has become so much richer as a result. I’m meeting interesting people every day, going to places I haven’t been before, and trying out new things. Last week I spent an evening at a small art gallery in Brunswick, another at a themed house party, and a morning at a philosophy reading group. I’m much happier than I was when I was scrolling Hinge. And I know something will happen when it’s meant to.
I’m learning that dating in a meaningful way takes courage, patience and rejection – like it did for generations before mine. In any case, I think I’d still rather be rejected in real life than do an internet stranger’s washing on a first date.
Saria Ratnam is a University of Melbourne arts student.
The Opinion newsletter is a weekly wrap of views that will challenge, champion and inform your own. Sign up here.

item.title: [cinemablend.com] Where All The Couples From 90 Day: The Last Resort Season 3 Ended Up
item.dc:creator: Mick Joest
item.description: 90 Day: The Last Resort Season 3 was one of the messiest iterations of the spinoff yet, with many 90 Day Fiancé couples at a breaking point in their marriage. As the show rounds out its time on the 2026 TV schedule, I'm sure many are wondering what's going on with them in the present and if any of their marriages survived the trials and ghosts of the castle. We learned a lot during the first part of the tell-all, and I was happy to see Ross Matthews back as host to ask some of the hard questions
item.content:encoded:
90 Day: The Last Resort Season 3 was one of the messiest iterations of the spinoff yet, with many 90 Day Fiancé couples at a breaking point in their marriage. As the show rounds out its time on the 2026 TV schedule, I'm sure many are wondering what's going on with them in the present and if any of their marriages survived the trials and ghosts of the castle.
We learned a lot during the first part of the tell-all, and I was happy to see Ross Matthews back as host to ask some of the hard questions. There's even some additional info to share based on what we've seen on social media, so let's dive in and give an update on where things stand.
Jenny And Sumit - Still Together
Jenny and Sumit Singh went into 90 Day: The Last Resort after a failed business endeavor in which they tried to open a cafe. In addition to being out of money, they had no means to move out of the home he shared with his parents. Jenny was tired of living with them, but Sumit was torn about breaking the tradition of living in a blended family household.
Since the tell-all was filmed, Jenny confirmed that Sumit's parents moved out. We also learned that she was diagnosed with ALS, and there are plans in place for her to seek treatment in the United States. Unfortunately, Sumit has had trouble obtaining a visa to be with her, and until that happens, Jenny seemingly wants to remain in India until he can travel with her. Here's hoping they can get some help soon.
Guillermo And Kara - No Longer Together
Kara Leona and Guillermo Rojer weren't together when they joined 90 Day: The Last Resort, but there was hope from at least one of them that they could salvage their marriage. Unfortunately, they were unable to reach a compromise when it came to Kara's explicit online content, and he ended up leaving the resort before the recommitment ceremony and left a letter saying that he couldn't make things work.
They continue to co-parent in the present, but the odds of them getting back together feel as though they are slim to none. Again, I can't say I'm surprised, because I already assumed the marriage was over before this season began, so it was more just further confirmation. We also know that Kara will appear in the spinoff 90 Day: Hunt For Love, so there's a possibility she'll continue to be involved in the franchise for a long time.
Russ And Pao - No Longer Together
Russ and Pao Mayfield were struggling in their marriage, as the latter wrestled with feeling she didn't have the support of a strong husband to lead their family. She felt as though she was doing most everything on her own, and he began to feel like an unnecessary component in her life. Despite that, they found some common ground and ultimately recommitted after he signed a contract freeing them from the responsibility of his financial issues.
Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News
A few weeks ago, Pao announced a split from Russ. It doesn't look like they'll reconcile either, but until the papers are officially signed, one can never say for sure. I felt they had the best chance of staying married out of everyone involved, but I guess it wasn't meant to be.
Shekinah And Sarper - No Longer Together
Shekinah and Sarper Güven were the highlight couple of the season, with the collapse of their marriage playing out in real time. Things really went downhill after Shekinah made an offensive comment to Thaís Ramone, and it felt like the arguments between them only escalated.
Their marital issues have continued to play out on social media, with Shekinah claiming Sarper is making offensive jokes about her in his stand-up comedy, and fans saying they're seeing him date others while on tour. Shekinah skipped coming to the tell-all, and it seems plausible we may never see her in 90 Day Fiancé again. As for Sarper, there are reports that he's filmed an additional spinoff appearance alongside Tyray Mollett, and I can't wait to see what that's about.
Patrick And Thaís - No Longer Together
Patrick Mendez and Thaís Ramone were going through a rough patch in their marriage, but it seemed they were one of the only couples who saw effective progress through marriage counseling. Granted, some would say there's no greater unifier between a couple than a shared enemy, and they both found that when Shekinah got into a fight with them.
As we learned during the 90 Day: The Last Resort tell-all, Patrick and Thaís filed for divorce. There was even some shock amongst the fandom when the details behind a domestic dispute came to light, though the charges were ultimately dropped. They ultimately decided the fighting in front of their daughter was not setting a good example, and it was best to split rather than let her see that.
Rebecca And Zied - No Longer Together
Zied Hakimi and Rebecca Parrott's troubles have been the same since they first arrived on 90 Day Fiancé, and The Last Resort didn't change anything. Rebecca was still convinced that Zied cheated on her, but had no solid evidence to prove it. Zied attempted to ease her fears after letting her look through his phone, but her constant need to do so made him feel trapped in the marriage.
We don't have explicit confirmation that Rebecca and Zied are no longer together, though it's heavily suspected following comments by her daughter-in-law suggesting they've split. Rebecca hasn't posted on Instagram since July, and Zied doesn't have any recent pictures of them together on his social media. I think it's safe to say either Rebecca's suspicions panned out, or maybe Zied just grew tired of constantly being accused of doing nothing.
90 Day: The Last Resort's episodes at the castle are over, but the drama lives on forever over on HBO Max. For those who haven't watched, it's certainly worth the time for anyone looking for some fun reality television.
Mick Joest is a Content Producer for CinemaBlend with his hand in an eclectic mix of television goodness. Star Trek is his main jam, but he also regularly reports on happenings in the world of Star Trek, WWE, Doctor Who, 90 Day Fiancé, Quantum Leap, and Big Brother. He graduated from the University of Southern Indiana with a degree in Journalism and a minor in Radio and Television. He's great at hosting panels and appearing on podcasts if given the chance as well.

item.content:encoded:
By Lee Minji
SEOUL, Sept. 22 (Yonhap) -- Korean auteur Lee Chang-dong is known for his grounded yet delicate portrayal of ordinary people, gradually unveiling them through the various layers that construct them rather than taking the easier way of labeling them.
The profound approach is epitomized in his Venice-winning masterpiece "Possible Love," his first feature in eight years since "Burning" (2018), which follows the lives of two married couples whose lives become intertwined in a way they had not imagined.
Their encounter takes place at a funeral for a laid-off worker who has taken his own life. The deceased is a former colleague of Ho-seok (Sul Kyung-gu), who had gone on strike against a mass layoff only to be brutally suppressed by police.
The traumatic experience still haunts Ho-seok, both mentally and physically, and as his wife Mi-ok (Jeon Do-yeon) gently reminds him not to drink alcohol, Ho-seok erupts into a fit of anger upon seeing documentary director Ye-ji (Cho Yeo-jeong) filming their conversation.
Meanwhile, as Mi-ok leaves the scene to get some fresh air, she runs into Ye-ji's husband, Sang-woo (Zo In-sung), as she searches for a loose wedding ring that escaped her finger. Unlike her brusque husband, Sang-woo appears tall, handsome and kind, as he moves his car to help her find the ring.
Following this encounter, Ye-ji is set on making Ho-seok the face of her documentary -- he has a sad face that only one person can have in the country, she tells Sang-woo -- and befriends Mi-ok, who seems more willing to speak on camera about the strike than her taciturn husband.
As their friendship deepens, Ye-ji and Sang-woo invite Mi-ok, Ho-seok and their young son Cheol to their fancy seaside home. Ho-seok, who first appears reluctant, eventually agrees to join them and even giving an interview on his experience.
But what seemed like a relaxed vacation at the picture-perfect estate -- which Mi-ok marvels at, describing it as a house that appears in a novel (to which Ho-seok responds: you don't read novels) -- sours in an unexpected direction as hidden desires and emotions surface.
At two hours and 44 minutes, "Possible Love" is not an easy watch. But Lee densely builds up the strength of the story in its nearly 3-hour run, weaving together unlikely themes, such as economic disparity, belonging and the moral boundary between a filmmaker and a subject.
The backbone of this process is the characters, whom Lee neither portrays in an obvious way nor turns them into subjects of mockery, while he does bring in moments of raw humor, such as when Mi-ok belts out an emotional trot song, to which Sang-woo plays the clarinet.
While Mi-ok is a working class mother who envies Ye-ji's luxury backpack and innocently raves about how much she adored Steve Jobs and how Sang-woo resembles him, she also has the dignity to tell Ye-ji that her stylish outfits are inappropriate for interacting with laid-off workers and their families. This side of Mi-ok comes to the fore in a symbolic seaside scene involving Sang-woo.
Sang-woo seems like a confident and compassionate person but the unseen hierarchy of power, deeply ingrained in his mind, is hinted by how he used to use a whistle as a child to call the family butler's son or how he tells Ye-ji she is "different" from the working-class couple.
In this film about filmmaking, Lee spends considerable time on depicting the agony of the laid-off workers who are called "the dead," in comparison with "the living," workers who managed to survive the layoff. He gives voices and faces to the laid-off workers in a counseling session scene where they take turns speaking on their emotions.
This part -- which Lee said he could not give up despite the risk of it making the film feel longer and duller -- perhaps serves as an answer to the underlying question of how filmmakers should treat the subjects of their films and whether their attempt to "love" them is possible or not.
Following a flurry of events, Mi-ok and Ho-seok return to their small home. Mi-ok complains that their home smells of trash but Ho-seok gently comforts her, saying that a little fresh air will clear the smell.
The film ends with a plainly elegant scene in which the couple sit in the moonlight, as they had as courting lovers, and share soju, leaving viewers a lingering trail of questions on the magnitude of money and class, but also a glimmering sense of relief on the possibility of love.
"Possible Love" is set for release Wednesday. It will be available on Netflix from Nov. 6.
mlee@yna.co.kr
(END)

item.content:encoded:
Dear Abby | Mom’s passing triggers reevaluation of friendships
Today's advice from Dear Abby.
DEAR ABBY: My mom died of extreme old age recently. She was a sweet woman everyone loved. I sent invitations to her memorial, and I’m getting a lot of excuses for why my friends can’t attend. I am upset.
In my circle of friends (all similar ages), I was the last to graduate, get a career job, start a relationship, buy a house, be married and so forth. I’ve attended my friends’ graduations, weddings, baby showers, milestone birthdays, and family funerals, yet there hasn’t been much reciprocation.
Excuses for not attending Mom’s memorial included going to a grandkid’s soccer game and attending a 2-year-old’s birthday party. Really? I know I’m dealing with unusually strong emotions due to Mom’s death, but I want to scream, “This is MY MOM,” not some distant friend or relative. My spouse says I shouldn’t stress and that all we need is each other (said by someone who has a huge, loving family whereas my family is just me and my dad). How do I deal with my feelings of resentment, abandonment and being a low priority?
— LAST ONE IN CALIFORNIA
DEAR LAST ONE: Your spouse is right. In the final analysis, all you need is each other — though a few supportive friends would certainly be welcome. I have always said that funerals are for the living, not the deceased. Be grateful for the support you are receiving from the people who accepted the invitation to your mother’s funeral. They are your core support group; the others are mere acquaintances, so start thinking of them in those terms.
** ** **
DEAR ABBY: I rent a two-bedroom apartment, which I shared with my best friend. When he moved away last month due to a work relocation, I advertised the room, and a couple moved in. They are friendly and pay their rent on time, but their cooking produces extremely strong smells that I cannot tolerate. My medication causes hypersensitivity to odors, and I can no longer stand to be in the kitchen because the smells linger. They also live on a very different schedule from me. As a result, my diet and sleep are both suffering. They remain unaware of how the adjustment has affected me because I don’t feel they are doing anything wrong. I would like to move out into a studio of my own. The lease on this apartment is currently a month-to-month, so the only thing keeping me here is the guilt I feel about burdening my roommates with this. They will have to move out, find a replacement for me or take on the full rent themselves. I want to do right by them, but I know it would be best for me to leave. What is the proper course of action here?
— DOOMED IN AUSTRALIA
DEAR DOOMED: There is no reason why you should feel guilty for leveling with this couple; your health must come first. Explain the problem to them and tell them that while you like them personally, your health is being affected by the cooking odors. Tell them that because you are now on a month-to-month lease, you plan to move to a smaller place of your own and give them the option of staying or moving. Consider this a first step in learning to stand up for yourself.

item.title: [bengals.com] Quick Hits | It's On To Pittsburgh for Cincinnati; From Reserve Ced Johnson To Rookie Cashius Howell, Bengals Find Pressure Points
item.dc:creator: Geoff Hobson
item.description: It just shows you the urgency of Steelers week at Paycor Stadium. item.content:encoded:
It just shows you the urgency of Steelers week at Paycor Stadium.
As Al Golden walked off the Reliant Stadium field Sunday with the biggest prize of his 19 games as the Bengals defensive coordinator, he looked like he was headed to a root canal instead of a locker room celebration.
The 2-0 Bengals head to Pittsburgh Sunday (1 p.m.-Cincinnati's Local 12), where the Steelers have amassed the only home winning percentage above 70% in the 57 seasons of the AFL-NFL merger.
"I was on to Pittsburgh. I know it's unfortunate. I mean, I was onto it. I was gone already," Golden told the media the Monday after his men hadn't allowed a touchdown in Houston.
Golden probably won't be soothed by Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow's 3-1 record in Pittsburgh and that he's won his last three starts at the Three Rivers. Instead, Golden is wondering, "What are they seeing? What we just saw? What are they seeing that fits with what they do and what are we going to see again? What do we need to stop?"
Golden even dropped his go-to quote from The Godfather.
"I know a lot of people want to stop and celebrate, but that's not the world that we've chosen," Golden said. "I say it all the time. Hyman Roth. This is the business we've chosen, and you've got to move on. And this league does not wait for anybody.
"This is the AFC North, this is the Pittsburgh Steelers in Pittsburgh, Aaron Rodgers, Mike McCarthy, we're moving on."
Short Yardage Goes Long Way
Golden may have a short memory, but he has great recall when it comes to Sunday's two biggest plays. Both coming on short yardage. Defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence II blew up a fourth-and-one at the Bengals 18 in a scoreless second quarter, and in the third quarter tackle T.J. Slaton stuffed a third-and-one that forced a short 58-yard field-goal try with the Bengals clinging to a 10-3 lead.
But Golden also saw a busy Demetrius Knight Jr., the linebacker who backed up both stops, as well as edge Cedric Johnson, safety Jordan Battle, and cornerback Dax Hill.
"Obviously, Dex did an awesome job on the first one. I think Ced Johnson setting the edge there on the first one, Jordan Battle fitting the C gap on the first one, and then (Knight) coming from the backside, that was really good.
"On the second one, it was a little bit of a different look and T.J. played into the tackle really well. Dax was on that side now as a corner and fit it really nice and we set the edge on that one as well."
Just Enough Ced
Speaking of Cedric Johnson, the third-year defensive end from Ole Miss, has four sacks in his last three games dating back to last season after Sunday's two. A sixth-round pick, Johnson was inactive for seven games as a rookie in 2024 and missed the first eight games last year with a calf injury.
But ever since he came back in a reserve role, all he does is produce. He recovered his first two career fumbles in the Thanksgiving Night win in Baltimore and hasn't stopped. He played 22 snaps that night and worked 23 Sunday in Houston after playing 19 in the opener. That was the second fewest in Sunday's line rotation. Only edge Shemar Stewart had fewer snaps (five) and he had a sack, too, as defensive line coach Jerry Montgomery went for the economy pack.
"You do (feel the rotation) because you just look at Shemar's sack. Shemar's fresh in the game, chipping the back and sees a gap and is able to explode through there because he's fresh," said head coach Zac Taylor Monday. "You're able to put fresh guys in the game at that moment. That's just so critical to be able to have that depth, keep those guys fresh over the course of the game, and not put too many snaps on them.
"And you're not taking them out because you feel like they need a breather, but you're worried about who's going in. We don't really have that concern now. Everybody's playing at a high level, and so we just got to keep that up."
Taylor, by the way, not only loves what Johnson has been giving them, but how.
"Ced's an easy guy to pull for because he just kind of goes about his business and is dependable and you've got to have those types of guys on your 53 and Ced has been one of those guys for us," Taylor said. "He's a really dependable player for us, and somebody we can count on. I thought he did a really good job in the run game last week against Tampa. This week he got to pay off in the pass game as well."
Cashing In On Cashius
Golden is still amazed the Bengals were able to draft Texas A&M edge Cashius Howell in the second round at No. 41 and rolled him out for 41 snaps, more than half the 80 plays. According to Pro Football Focus, Howell had seven pressures in a game the web site ticketed the Bengals for 44 with an astounding 54.5% win rate.
When Johnson racked up the last "coffin nails," sack, it was Howell, just missing his first NFL sack, who set him up with a clean shot off the edge against left tackle Aireontae Ersery as part of a three-man rush. Howell also battled with 380-pound right tackle Trent Brown, despite a weight difference of about 130 pounds or so.
"No, he didn't," said Howell, when asked if Golden gave him a number of pressures. "But I'll take one if you got it."
Told it was about five pressures and maybe more, Howell thought and said, "Let's do that for at least 15 more weeks."
"As a rusher, he knows exactly who he is. He's got a speed, he's got a dip, he's got to counter off that," Golden said. "That's three, that's all he needs. He plays with a high motor. I thought he set the edge really well for us (Sunday), especially as big as Trenton is. And then he gives you two, three drops a game, which is awesome. It just makes us so much more versatile. And he's doing all those things for us right now, which is great."
Howell said last Friday that he needed to improve his quickness off the snap.
"Nothing specific, but just being intentional about it over the course of the week at practice," Howell said. "Keep loading up that front foot and just getting off the ball."
Slants and Screens
Asked what Burrow's practice status is this week after going full only once last week with a tight back, Taylor offered, "I think I know the answer to that, but I don't want to give you that right now." …
Knight tied his career-high with 12 tackles and got a game ball. His traveling leather cowboy hat was a perfect match, but he didn't buy it just for the Houston trip. "I'm a hat guy," Knight said. "I bought it first thing in the offseason."
He also wore cowboy boots on the way in, but he carried them back home: "Not after playing a three-hour football game." …
Knight's 19 tackles are seven away from Titans linebacker Anthony Hill's NFL-leading 26 …
Everything went right for the Bengals' special teams Sunday. Kicker Evan McPherson perfect from beyond 50 yards. Four Ryan Rehkow punts inside the 20. Seven Texans drive starts inside the 25.
And they camethisclose to an opening kick return touchdown by wide receiver Dohnte Meyers. Meyers looked like he was headed there in his second NFL game when he stumbled after his career-long 40-yarder.
"I saw a lot of daylight. I know that. It was perfectly blocked. I just followed the way it was drawn up," Meyers said. "I think my eyes and my mind saw it before my feet did. That was not a good combination." …
Meyers is showing why they tapped him to replace Charlie Jones as the primary returner. He's shown soft hands catching punts and has displayed a knack for coming up and making catches before they bounce.
"I think I was too deep on a couple, but I'm comfortable back there," Meyers said …

item.content:encoded:
Ha-Chan, Shake Your Booty!, 2026.
Directed by Josef Kubota Wladyka.
Starring Rinko Kikuchi, Alberto Guerra, Alejandro Edda, You, Yoh Yoshida, Charley Flyte, Soji Arai, Chelsea Gonzalez, Derek Mio, and Damián Alcázar.
SYNOPSIS:
Haru and Luis love competing in Tokyo’s ballroom dance scene, but after tragedy strikes, Haru withdraws into isolation. When friends coax her back to the studio, she develops an infatuation with the new instructor.
Everything from an exploration of the powerful connectivity of music and dance transcending language (there is a combination of Japanese, Spanish, and English here all distinctly colored and stylized for clarity), open relationships, and a fantastical study of grief, co-writer/director Josef Kubota Wladyka (penning the screenplay alongside Nicholas Huynh, the movie is dedicated to the filmmaker’s dancer mother) Ha-Chan, Shake Your Booty! is a strange film that will work one moment and possibly feel a bit too whimsical or odd the next.
With a slightly overlong opening, the filmmakers introduce viewers to the lives of Haru (Rinko Kikuchi) and Luis (Alejandro Edda), a rumba-dancing married couple living a quiet, happy life before the latter has a heart attack during their routine lessons. Even nine months removed from Luis’ death, Haru is living in isolation and won’t even come out of the house to celebrate her birthday. She has also started hallucinating seeing Luis at night inside of a black bird costume, no doubt symbolizing the grief she can’t move on from.
Eventually, her friends have had enough of this and basically force her out of the house (one is dialed back, the other is horny and obsessed with sleeping around through dating apps) to take up more dancing lessons, where the three of them come into the sphere of instructor Fedir (Alberto Guerra), absurdly attractive and accomplished but also married. However, after some digging by Haru’s relatives, they learn that he is in an open marriage, which prompts her to research this dynamic, which appears to be unheard of in Japanese culture. Understandably, Haru seems to think all of this is crazy, but she also appears to view Fedir as a potential replacement for her lost love.
In secret, away from her friends, Haru makes her move on Fedir, which allows the film to enter its magical musical groove, complete with imaginative sequences, such as one in which a fight against some street hoodlums harassing the woman transitions into a blend of punches and dance choreography. Another winning moment sees Haru take Fedir to a Japanese dance show, where Fedir is unsure whether he will understand what is happening. That is, until everything breaks out into numbers set to music from Dirty Dancing (if it wasn’t obvious by now, the soundtrack here is wonderful, with Japanese arrangements of well-known Western songs).
From the bright color palette to the costume to the choreography itself, those segments are what give the film most of its charm. In trying to function as a lighthearted take on grief and reinvigoration through life and art, there are also some interesting points made about love and the reactions of those who are in love with someone else. There are reservations to be had about where the open marriage aspect ultimately goes, but Ha-Chan, Shake Your Booty! remains an idiosyncratic, intentionally messy (just like life), and uplifting look at moving on. The dramatic beats don’t always click, but it is vibrantly acted with equally rising musical numbers and undeniable inventiveness at the helm in director Josef Kubota Wladyka.
Flickering Myth Rating – Film: ★ ★ ★ / Movie: ★ ★ ★
Robert Kojder

Love Horoscope Today for Tuesday, September 22, 2026: Leo Signs Should Be Cautious in Relationships, Know the Status of Other Signs
Love Life Predictions for September 22, 2026: Personal relationships for Leo signs will remain normal. However, caution will be necessary in relationships. Maintain harmony with close ones and friends. You will progress through mutual support and listen to your loved ones.
Aries
Aries individuals will experience mutual trust within the family. The emotional aspect will be strong, and there will be opportunities to share happiness with family members. The home atmosphere will be filled with joy and delight. Loved ones will be pleased, and mutual trust will increase. You will make efforts for your close ones. Harmony will be maintained in relationships, and partners will be supportive.
Taurus
Taurus individuals may meet a loved one. Behaviour will become sweeter, and there will be many opportunities for conversation. The home environment will be favourable. Close ones will be happy. The situation in emotional matters will improve. Success in romantic relationships is possible, and there will be a chance to express your feelings. Positive energy will remain in relationships.
Gemini
Gemini individuals need to maintain enthusiasm in personal matters. Proceed with humility and discretion. Avoid rushing in matters connected to the heart. Attention will be on personal relationships, and friends will offer support. You will share joys and sorrows with loved ones. It will be important to control emotions. During this time, you may also receive important information.
Cancer
Cancer individuals will have a strong emotional side. Interest in socialising will increase, and there will be opportunities to spend pleasant time with close ones. Happiness will increase at home. Love and trust will remain in married life. Good proposals may come. It will be important to maintain confidentiality in personal matters. You will succeed in gaining the trust of close ones.
Leo
Leo individuals should try to increase the happiness of loved ones through love and affection. Personal relationships will remain normal. However, caution will be necessary in relationships. Maintain harmony with close ones and friends. You will progress through mutual help and listen to your loved ones. Do not rush to express your feelings; wait for the right opportunity.
Virgo
Virgo individuals will focus on increasing the happiness of loved ones. Good news may come from friends. The romantic side will improve, and there will be meetings with loved ones. Respect for experienced people will be maintained. Personal matters will be organised, and harmony will be maintained with everyone. The atmosphere at home will be joyful. Opportunities for outings and entertainment may also arise.
Libra
Libra individuals need to maintain cooperation and trust with everyone. Increase humility in discussions and dialogue. It will be better for relationships to overlook minor issues. Maintain balance in emotional matters. You will try to increase socialising with close ones. You will welcome guests at home and listen carefully to your loved ones.
Scorpio
Scorpio individuals may experience increased sweetness in romantic relationships. Enthusiasm will remain during meetings, and relationships will be comfortable. You will share happiness with loved ones. You will be natural in emotional matters. Opportunities for pleasant conversations will arise. There will be ease in expressing love. Paying attention to relationships will strengthen mutual trust.
Sagittarius
Sagittarius individuals will stay connected with loved ones and may receive desired support. Focus will be on maintaining relationships and fulfilling promises made. Harmony will be maintained with everyone. Situations in love and emotional matters may be favourable. There will be meetings with friends, and closeness with family members will increase.
Capricorn
Capricorn individuals may experience pleasant moments related to love and affection. There will be good meetings with loved ones, and sweetness in relationships will increase. With improvements in relationships, mutual attraction will remain. Relationships with friends will strengthen. Joint efforts will gain momentum. Love and harmony will increase. Good proposals may receive support. Respect for elders should be maintained.
Aquarius
Aquarius individuals should overlook the shortcomings of close ones. Maintain ease in love and behaviour. Focus on improving contact and communication. Relationships with friends will strengthen. You will take time for loved ones and create opportunities to meet. Avoid boastfulness and showiness. It will be important to remain patient and cautious in relationships.
Pisces
Pisces individuals will have favourable domestic matters. There will be ease in expressing emotions, and heartfelt relationships will strengthen. You will be effective in conversations and will strive to improve relationships. Confidence will increase. Trust in romantic relationships will grow. Opportunities for outings and entertainment with loved ones will arise. All family members will be supportive.

Offset will be taking your calls — sort of.
In an Instagram post shared on Tuesday (Sep. 15), the rapper announced the launch of NEED FM, which appeared to be a late-night advice hotline for anyone in need of answers.
The post is accompanied by a phone number, 470-742-6949. However, a call will not lead to a chance to have a conversation with Offset about your love life. Instead, it will trigger a text message with a pre-save link for his upcoming single "Something I Need."
COMPLEX SHOP: Shop the brands you love, anytime and anywhere. Uncover what's next. Buy. Collect. Obsess.
While a new single from Offset is on the horizon, Quavo recently confirmed the two will reunite for a final Migos album and tour.
"We coming back," Quavo told DJ Greg Street on the Atlanta radio station V-103. "We're going to do it one more time."
It's uncertain if this new Migos album will feature posthumous contributions from Takeoff, who fatally shot in Houston four years ago.
The announcement of a new Migos album comes months after Quavo posted a photo of himself and Takeoff and hinted at a reunion, writing, "AINT NO NEW CHAPTER JUST THE NEXT ONE!!!"
Offset followed up with a photo of the trio around the time of 2021's Culture III, with the caption, "On dat!!!!"
Following the release of Culture III, tensions between Offset and Quavo caused them to part ways. The two set their differences aside and took the stage together for a tribute to Takeoff at the 2023 BET Awards.
Offset indicated on 7PM in Brooklyn With Carmelo Anthony that he and Quavo were in a better place and were speaking somewhat regularly.

item.title: [vogue.com] The Bride Wore a Pearlescent, Ocean-Inspired Wardrobe for Her Harbour Island Wedding
item.dc:creator: Shelby Wax
item.description: A game of truth or dare led high school best friends Bella Pepin and Cameron Kenny to realize they should be something more. “But my junior year and his senior year, everything changed,” Bella recalls. The two were dared to kiss each other at a Halloween party, and they automatically felt a spark. “We started dating pretty much immediately and dated through the rest of high school and throughout college with a few on-and-offs,” says Bella. After college, the two Florida natives drifted apart and
item.content:encoded:
A game of truth or dare led high school best friends Bella Pepin and Cameron Kenny to realize they should be something more. “But my junior year and his senior year, everything changed,” Bella recalls. The two were dared to kiss each other at a Halloween party, and they automatically felt a spark. “We started dating pretty much immediately and dated through the rest of high school and throughout college with a few on-and-offs,” says Bella. After college, the two Florida natives drifted apart and didn’t see each other for five years. A chance meeting at a bar out in Montauk changed their fate. “We were too nervous to say hi to each other for over an hour or so,” she shares. “Eventually, we briefly chatted, but nothing came of that night!” Back in NYC, Bella decided to be forward and ask Cameron to grab coffee. “We ended up walking six miles in circles on the West Side Highway, catching up on the last five years of life. It felt like we picked back up right where we left off,” she shares. “We were so young when we first dated, so the time apart really allowed us to grow up and learn ourselves. Getting back together this time, we both knew it was for good.”
Two years later, the couple moved in together in Dallas with a golden retriever named Goose and a cat named Rigatoni. The following spring, Cameron proposed to Bella on his 31st birthday while they were on a trip together on Harbour Island, a place he has traveled to with his family for years. “He waited until the second night of the trip to propose—which really threw me off,” says Bella. The two were walking on the beach to dinner at sunset when Cameron popped the question as a hidden photographer captured the moment. The two continued the night with celebrations at dinner and calls with their families to tell them the news. “That same weekend, Cameron wasted no time and surprised me with a tour of The Other Side—our wedding venue,” says Bella. “It was full speed ahead!”
The two decided to have their friends and family join them for their Bahamas destination wedding on April 11, 2026. “There is something really special about it,” Bella says of Harbour Island. “We love the relaxed yet refined vibe, the food, the design, and the people… We never considered a wedding anywhere else.” Bella, who works as an interior designer, partnered up with their wedding planner Sophia Goff to execute their vision. “Sophia is a creative genius, and we immediately clicked,” she says. “Knowing how much I cared, she let me into the weeds with her—reviewing fabric samples and tabletop tailoring details and so much more. I’m so grateful she brought me behind the scenes.” The groom gives the two all the credit. Cameron adds, “I only helped manage the band and requested no lines at any bars!”
The vision for the weekend was to have a unique, elevated design perspective, without it feeling too serious. “Island-y, but not beach-y,” explains Bella. “All of our events were outdoors—with the exception of a rehearsal dinner pivot due to rain—so we wanted the designs to mimic natural Caribbean elements, sticking to a color and material palette seen in the surrounding tropical landscape.” The bride also put particular care into the invitations and paper goods throughout the weekend, hiring calligrapher Emily Snyder to create playful illustrations for the designs. The bride adds, “The kissing fish she doodled are everything to me!”
This design ethos also translated into Bella’s style choices for the weekend. “I wanted my wardrobe to feel classic, yet fun with loads of island influence,” she says. “The location lent itself to lots of texture and fun accessorizing—raffia fringe, sheer materials, floral appliqués, pearls, shells, and fish!” The bride credits her friend, stylist Madison Childs Lee, as a major help in curating her weekend ensembles. “She innately has a really cool eye, is a master at sourcing unique pieces, and helped me pull together the final touches on each look,” Bella shares.
The bride kicked off the weekend in a Danielle Frankel gown with hand-painted appliqués and baroque pearl tendrils for the rehearsal dinner. “I felt like a mermaid that just came from the sea,” she reminisces. For the beach day, Bella donned a sheer, lacework dress from Matin’s fall collection. She adds, “I think I saw a runway photo of it on their Instagram, and knew I needed it for the weekend!” The welcome party look by Holli Studio was one of the bride’s favorites. “The butter leather top and skirt with raffia fringe didn’t feel overly bridal and were so fun and flirty to wear,” she says. “I can't wait to rewear it.” Bella paired the set with a silver and pearl shell necklace her mom bought on her honeymoon in St. Croix in the ’80s. “Immediate prized possession status,” she adds.
For her trip down the aisle, the bride wore Danielle Frankel’s Arlo gown, a high-neck silk wool dress with pearl-like sheen, a low back, and raw chiffon trim. “I knew I wanted to be a Danielle Frankel bride, so much so that I didn’t try on any other bridal lines,” she says. “I worked with the team at the NYC studio on custom additions, and we ended up adding more of the raw chiffon material around the bust and down the waist. I love the added texture and airiness it gave the look.” She paired the look with a custom shell pouch from the brand by Sloan and custom diamond and pearl earrings by her friend Lili George made to mimic an Art Deco pair she once saw at an estate sale. “They added a touch of old-world to the look and I’ll cherish them forever,” Bella gushes.
Cameron kept his wedding weekend looks classic in custom suiting by P Johnson and Sid Mashburn. Tones of the looks were in blues, greens, and neutrals to mirror the design palette. “For the wedding day, he wanted to wear an ivory dinner jacket as a nod to what he wore when he took me to his senior prom,” shares Bella. “He wore cufflinks engraved with our initials gifted by me on wedding day, and black raffia loafers to give the look a bit more of an island feel.” She adds, “He looked so handsome.”
The weekend kicked off with a rehearsal dinner filled with speeches and classic Bahamian dishes served family style. “The interior design style of Pink Sands Hotel feels very British West Indies, so we leaned in,” shares the bride. “We had to move the dinner from their garden into the restaurant at the last minute due to rain, but I honestly think being inside the hotel gave more context to our design.” The night ended at a dive bar named Gusty’s complete with a disco ball and never-ending early-2000s hits. “We stayed out later than planned, but it was so much fun,” says Bella.
The following day, guests hit the beach at Ms. V’s and enjoyed painkillers, local beer, and fish sandwiches. “It was so fun to be hanging on the beach, sunning and swimming with all of our people in a more casual setting before the wedding events kicked off,” shares the bride. That night, the welcome party at Coral Sands Hotel’s Beach Bar was a “full-on shell explosion.” Custom coasters, aprons, menus, and mosaics all featured shell motifs. “We wanted to be super playful to go with the loud and punchy decor of the hotel,” Bella says.
The bride and groom spurred tradition and saw each other the morning of the wedding for a sunrise swim in the ocean. “It was the highlight of the weekend for me,” shares Bella. “Break the rules! See each other before the wedding!” As the ceremony approached, windy weather led to some last-minute changes. “I started with my hair styled down and 10 minutes before walking down the aisle, Alejandra threw it up into a bun,” says the bride. “We also ended up flipping the ceremony seating so guests were facing away from the ocean to avoid wind feedback on the mic. You can only plan for so much!”
The couple legally tied the knot in their hometown in Florida five months earlier, which helped shed some of the nerves around the ceremony. “I think we both felt more excited than nervous,” says the bride. “Cameron’s uncle Davis officiated, and we recited our own personal vows, which were very teary. How can you put a 15-year-long journey into two minutes?!” The newlyweds recessed to “Oh La La” by Faces and felt like they were in a movie. “We had a sweet moment to ourselves and cheersed with a spritz before joining the guests at cocktails on the lawn,” remembers Bella.
The cocktail and reception spaces were filled with native plants and overgrown florals. “The Other Side has a very weathered and wild vibe to it, and Sophia and I kept coming back to this idea of a deserted island,” says Bella. “But, of course, [we had] a really chic dressed-up dinner with silk taffeta table linens for a bit of unexpected fancy. It was black tie after all.”
Before dinner, the couple shared their first dance to “Cruisin’” by Smokey Robinson. “My mom raised my sisters and I on soul and Motown, and I’ve always loved this song. But now it holds a bigger meaning for us,” says the bride. Cameron danced to “In My Life” by The Beatles with his mother, and Bella’s father gave a speech with a Phil Collins-inspired intro. “It was nothing short of iconic, and got the crowd on their feet,” she shares.
The bride changed into a TWP strapless dress and shell necklace as the dancing really kicked off. The band played a curated setlist that kept the dance floor packed all night. Cameron notes, “It was electric!” The night transitioned to the after-party complete with a DJ and live saxophone player. “The groomsmen had my dad on their shoulders at one point, and even my 11-year-old sister stayed ‘til the early morning hours,” says Bella. “We never wanted it to end!”
Reflecting on the weekend, the bride says, “We’re just so happy, and everything felt so authentically us: the design, place, the music, our people, all of it.” Adds the groom, “I wouldn’t change a thing! I wish we could do it all again.”

item.title: [cosmopolitan.com] A Full Guide to All Four Attachment Styles, According to Experts
item.dc:creator: Rachel Varina
item.description: If you’ve ever wondered why you’re perfectly chill when someone you’re dating takes three hours to text back while your best friend is already drafting a “so I guess you hate me?” follow-up after 20 minutes, attachment styles might have something to do with it. item.content:encoded:
If you’ve ever wondered why you’re perfectly chill when someone you’re dating takes three hours to text back while your best friend is already drafting a “so I guess you hate me?” follow-up after 20 minutes, attachment styles might have something to do with it. Or maybe you’re the one who starts feeling vaguely trapped the second someone gets a little too close. Also potentially an attachment thing!
Basically, attachment styles describe some of the ways we navigate emotional connections with other people. “Attachment theory sheds light on how humans form and maintain emotional bonds,” explains relationship and EMDR therapist Ashley Starwood, LCSW. The theory, originally developed by psychologists John Bowlby and Mary Ainsworth, suggests that our earliest relationships with parents or caregivers can influence how we approach relationships later in life.
There are four main attachment styles: secure, anxious, avoidant, and disorganized (also known as fearful-avoidant). And while figuring out yours might explain a thing or two about why you act the way you do when feelings get involved, it’s not a diagnosis or some permanent relationship fate you’re stuck with forever. You can even experience different attachment patterns with different people.
So, yes, there may actually be a reason you’re drawn to people who make you want to throw your phone into the ocean. Ahead, experts break down what each attachment style means, where it comes from, how it can affect your relationships, and whether you can change yours.
How Are Attachment Styles Formed?
Attachment styles are largely shaped by early childhood experiences. “Your parents’ ability to be attuned to your needs and be emotionally safe caregivers greatly impacts your ability to build secure attachment,” says Morgan Anderson, PsyD, an attachment theory expert and author of Love Magnet. For example, caregivers who consistently and compassionately meet their child’s needs can help foster a sense of trust. “Conversely, inconsistent, neglectful, or even abusive caregiving can create feelings of insecurity, anxiety, or fear in the child,” adds Starwood.
But your parents or caregivers aren’t the only relationships that can shape your attachment patterns. Anderson says early non-familial relationships can play a role, too, and experiences later in life can also affect how you approach relationships. According to eharmony’s September 2023 Dating Diaries report, for example, 84 percent of Gen Z singles said past heartbreaks had made them “more cautious” about relationships, while 72 percent said they’d become “less trusting,” notes eharmony relationship expert Laurel House.
Your attachment style isn’t necessarily identical in every relationship, either. You might feel more secure with some people and more anxious, avoidant, or fearful-avoidant with others. Your partner’s attachment style can influence the dynamic between you, as can your current circumstances and feelings of self-worth.
Secure Attachment
As the name suggests, someone with a secure attachment style generally feels, well, secure in forming and maintaining healthy relationships. They tend to value closeness in their relationships, Anderson explains, but also know how to set healthy boundaries and communicate their needs effectively. “In securely-attached relationships, partners experience ‘interdependence,’ meaning they are able to practice self-soothing simultaneously and can also ask their partner for support and reassurance,” she says.
How it’s formed: House says caregivers who are consistently present and responsive to their child’s needs within the first year of life and beyond can help foster secure attachment.
Anxious Attachment
While someone with an anxious attachment style may crave closeness with their partner, Starwood says they often have a deep-seated fear of abandonment and rejection. They may frequently seek reassurance from their partners but struggle to actually believe or internalize it when they get it.
“With anxious attachment, there is often coping through excessive communication, becoming a ‘chameleon’ in your relationships, passive expression of needs, and even codependency,” Anderson explains. “Unconsciously, the anxiously attached person is thinking, I will do anything not to be abandoned.”
How it’s formed: “Emotionally inconsistent and unpredictable caregivers contribute to creating adults with anxious relationships,” says House. Parents who are sometimes available and sometimes distant can lead to children (and eventually, adults) who feel anxious about future connections.
Avoidant Attachment
Think of avoidant attachment as pretty much the polar opposite of anxious attachment. Instead of craving constant reassurance, someone with an avoidant attachment style tends to value hyper-independence and may feel uncomfortable with closeness. “If you have an avoidant attachment style, you struggle to be vulnerable in your relationships and may find yourself pulling away from people,” Anderson explains. “Avoidantly-attached individuals still crave intimacy, but their fear of it outweighs their desire to be close. There is often a lack of emotional awareness with avoidant attachment, meaning these individuals are not connected to their own emotional experience, which in turn makes it nearly impossible for them to connect to the emotional experience of others.”
How it’s formed: Dismissive, disconnected, or distant caregiving can contribute to avoidant attachment, House says. When children’s emotional needs aren’t consistently met within their relationships, they may learn to rely primarily on themselves.
Disorganized Attachment
The final attachment style is disorganized, also known as fearful-avoidant (FA), and according to Anderson, it’s often linked to childhood trauma. “An individual with an FA attachment style experiences both anxious and avoidant strategies simultaneously,” she says. “This can manifest as a pendulum swinging from fear of abandonment to desiring complete independence. Those with a fearful-avoidant attachment style have a hard time trusting anyone and struggle to form lasting relationships.”
How it’s formed: Disorganized attachment can develop in highly unpredictable or abusive environments. “Fearful-avoidant attachment is characterized by inconsistent or unpredictable caregiving experiences,” Starwood explains. “It involves a mix of behaviors, where a child might seek closeness but then become withdrawn or fearful, reflecting the instability they experience at home.”
How to Figure Out Your Attachment Style
Maybe one of those descriptions just gave you a major lightbulb moment. Or maybe you read all four and are still sitting here like, okay, but which one am I? If you’re not sure, Starwood suggests reflecting on your childhood, experiences with caregivers, and past relationships, paying attention to how each may have affected your sense of security and trust.
There are also online tests that can help you explore your attachment style. You can try this attachment style quiz from the Attachment Project or Anderson’s five-minute attachment style questionnaire. Whichever you take, Starwood stresses that the results should be considered a starting point rather than a definitive answer.
“A psychotherapist can provide a more in-depth assessment of your attachment style using standardized tools and clinical interviews,” she says. “This can be particularly helpful if you're interested in a deeper understanding of your attachment patterns and how they might impact your relationships.”
How to Change Your Attachment Style
Good news: Your attachment style isn’t set in stone. Even if certain patterns have been with you since childhood, it’s possible to develop healthier, more secure ways of relating to other people. The first step, Anderson says, is understanding the patterns you tend to fall into. “It starts with awareness, followed by actively releasing outdated patterns through emotional regulation and secure relationship skills like assertive communication and setting boundaries.”
Therapy can also help, says Starwood, especially if you’re trying to understand where certain patterns come from and develop new ways of responding to them. Depending on what you’re working through, that might mean learning to communicate your needs more directly, set boundaries, regulate difficult emotions, or feel more comfortable with intimacy.
And don’t expect your attachment patterns to change overnight. “Celebrate your progress, no matter how small, and be patient with yourself,” Starwood says. Becoming more secure is less about suddenly transforming into a completely different person and more about noticing old patterns and gradually learning how to respond differently.
Ultimately, knowing your attachment style isn’t about putting yourself into a box. It’s about understanding yourself—and your relationships—a little better, then deciding what, if anything, you’d like to do differently going forward.

item.title: [cosmopolitan.com] The 15 Best Dating Apps for Serious Relationships
item.dc:creator: Rachel Varina; Sophie Saint Thomas
item.description: If you’re looking for a serious relationship, dating apps can start to feel like a particularly exhausting game of “What the hell are you actually looking for?” Sure, their profile says “long-term relationship,” but does that mean marriage?
